title: Steps to Install SIM Card
discription:
To ensure a smooth initial setup of your device, follow these steps to correctly insert the SIM card:

rnrn

1. Open Flap: Locate the E-101 side flap on your device. Gently pull it out using the knob attached to the flap.
rn2. Insert SIM in SIM Port: Place the SIM card into the designated slot as illustrated in the device manual. Ensure that the cut-off corner of the SIM card is aligned correctly and pointing forward towards the slot.
rn3. ON/OFF Switch: After inserting the SIM, turn on the switch to operate the device.
rn4 . Close the Flap: Once the device is switched on after inserting the SIM, carefully reinsert the flap until it is securely closed.

rnrn

The device is now ready to be connected and powered on:

rnrn

rnrn

 SIM card insertion/removal must be performed when device is powered off – external voltage disconnected and Switch is OFF. Otherwise SIM card might be damaged or device will not detect it.

title: Quick SMS Configuration
discription:
The default configuration ensures optimal track quality and efficient data usage. Follow these steps to quickly set up your device via SMS commands.

rnrn

A. Commands to Change Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To port the device to a SERVER
rn- Command: #SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;
rn- Example: #SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000; <6906>
rn- Description: This command directs the EL-100 device to connect to the server specified by the given IP address and port number. In the example, the device will be configured to communicate with the server at IP 196.168.175.12 and port 20000.

rnrn

2. To change the APN settings
rn- Command: #CONFIG::APN::username::password;
rn- Purpose: Configures your GPRS account settings.
rn- Details:

rnrn

- APN (Access Point Name): Used to access the GPRS gateway provided by your network operator.
rn- Username: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).
rn- Password: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).
rn- Example: For the Idea network without internet, the command would be: #CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>

rnrn

3. PPI Configuration
rn- Command: WEBSTART,
rn- Purpose: Command to set the tracking interval and you will get confirmation SMS and then start sending data to our web server, where xxx stands for active(IGN ON) interval, yyy stands for passive(IGN OFF) interval, zzz stands for Main Power Removal interval and z1z1z1 stands for panic interval. H - Hours, M-Minutes, S- Seconds
rn- Example: WEBSTART030S,030S,030S,030S<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Commands to Check Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Check the GPRS Status
rn- Command: GPRSSTATUS<6906>
rn- Purpose: Retrieves the complete status of the device.

2. To Get GPS Details

rnrn

Send the command `GETGPS` to the EL-100 device.

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are unreachable: You will receive the message "GPS NOT FOUND."
rn- If GPS satellites are reachable: You will receive a web link to view the location on a map.

rnrn

Additionally, you will receive the following information:
rn- Speed: Indicates the speed of the vehicle in KPH.
rn- Date: The date of the recorded data.
rn- Time: The time of the recorded data in IST.

rnrn

To view the exact location on Google Maps, enter the latitude and longitude coordinates separated by a comma (,) in the search bar at [www.maps.google.com](http://www.maps.google.com). This will show the precise location
rnon the map.

rnrn

3.To Check the Status of the System
rnCommand: SYSSTATUS<6906>
rnResponse: This command provides important system statuses, including:
rn- Main power status
rn- Ignition status
rn- Immobilizer status
rn- PANIC status
rn- No Meaning
rn- Reserved field
rn- Odometer (KM)
rn- Onboard temperature
rn- Internal battery voltage
rn- O/P2 Status

rnrn

C. FE<6906>: 

rnrn

This Command is used to clear the unsent memory data from flash.

rnrn

 

rnrn

D. FR<6906>:

rnrn

This Command is used to set factory default values. After this, all the user configured settings will be erased and factory fitted values will be implemented.

rnrn

 

rnrn

E. Default Configuration Settings

rnrn

1. Movement and Ignition Detection

rnrn

- Movement Detection: The device detects vehicle movement using the accelerometer.
rn- Ignition Detection: The ignition is detected by the vehicle's power voltage, which should range between 8 and 90 volts.

rnrn

2. Device Recording on Movement
rn- Recording Conditions: When the vehicle covers a distance of at least 50 meters while in idle mode, the device will begin tracking the movement of the vehicle.
rn- Stop Detection: The device will mark the vehicle as stopped if it remains stationary for one continuous minute.

rnrn

3. Device Recording on Stop
rn- Recording Conditions: If the vehicle remains stationary for one continuous minute, the device will mark it as stopped.(Speed 0kmph and no signal from motion sensors/accelerometer)

rnrn

4. Sending Records to Server
rn- Data Transmission: Once a record is made, it is sent to the server according to the default settings. Data can be sent based on specific criteria such as set time intervals, alerts, angle changes, and distance traveled.

rnrn

5. Synchronization and Updates
rnAfter a successful SMS configuration, the EL-100 device will synchronize its time and update the records to the configured server. Users can modify time intervals and default I/O elements using the Atlanta Configurator tool or additional SMS commands. This ensures that the device remains accurate and up-to-date, providing reliable data for monitoring vehicle movement and status.

title: Mounting Guidelines
discription:
1. Connecting Wires

rnrn

- Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.
rn- Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.
rn- Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.
rn- Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source

rnrn

- Power Retention During Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.
rn- Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.
rn- Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and rotection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire

rnrn

- Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.
rn- Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.
rn- Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire

rnrn

- Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.
rn- Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.
rn- Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

Relay Wiring Diagram Explanation

rnrn

rnrn

To properly connect the relay for your device, follow these detailed instructions:
rn1. Pin 85
rnConnect the wire on pin 85 pin with the power source. Ensure that the power supply voltage matches the voltage requirements of your vehicle.
rn
rn2. Pin 87A (Normally Closed) and Pin 30 (Common Connection)
rn- Pin 30: You need to cut the vehicle’s ignition wire and connect one end to Pin 87A and connect ignition sense wire of the device.
rn- Pin 87A: Connect it to the ACC (Accessory), Vehicles/ Key Switch wire of your vehicle.
rn
rn3. Pin 86
rnConnect this pin to the device's ignition control wire. This wire controls the relay’s switching based on the ignition status.
rn
rnBy following these connections, you ensure that the relay is correctly wired to manage the ignition and power supply for your device, allowing for proper operation and control.

rnrn

 

rnrn

NOTE: Power Supply Connection Guidelines

rnrn

Optimal Connection Point
rnWhen connecting the power supply for the E-101 device, it is crucial to select a point with very low impedance on the vehicle's onboard network. Such points are typically found at the battery terminals of the car. This ensures stable voltage supply and minimizes the risk of electrical interference.
rn
rnRecommended Connection Methods
rn1. Direct Battery Terminal Connection: It is highly recommended to connect the E-101's power wires (GND and POWER) directly to the battery terminals. This direct connection provides a reliable and stable power source for the device.
rn2. Fuse Box Connection: Alternatively, you can connect the wires to the main POWER cable inside the vehicle's fuse box. Ensure that the fuse box is connected to the vehicle's computer power supply. This method also provides a controlled power supply environment.
rn
rnGround Connection Considerations
rn- GND Wire Connection: The GND wire must be connected to a designated point specifically designed for connecting vehicle computer grounds. Avoid arbitrary grounding to the car's mass, as this can introduce unpredictable static and dynamic potentials, potentially leading to unstable operation or failure of the E-101 device.
rn
rnBy adhering to these detailed connection guidelines, you can ensure the proper and reliable operation of the E-101 device within your vehicle's electrical system. Always prioritize stable connections and avoid any practices that could compromise the device's performance or safety.

rn

title: Safety Instructions
discription:
Operating the E-101 device safely requires careful attention to the following guidelines and recommendations. Adhering to these instructions will help you avoid hazardous situations and ensure the optimal performance of your device. Please read and follow these instructions meticulously before operating the device.

rnrn

A. Safety instructions

rnrn

1. Power Specifications
rn- The E-101 device operates on a nominal voltage of +12 V DC/+24 V DC.
rn- The allowable voltage range for safe operation is between +8 V DC and +36 V DC.
rn
rn2. Transportation and Handling
rn- To prevent mechanical damage during transportation, ensure that the device is packaged in an impact-resistant container.
rn- When setting up the device, place it in a location where the LED indicators are clearly visible. These indicators provide essential information about the device's operational status.
rn
rn3. Connection and Disconnection Procedures
rn- When connecting the 1x4 cables to the vehicle, make sure to disconnect the relevant jumpers from the vehicle's power supply first.
rn- Before removing the device from the vehicle, always disconnect the 1x4 connection to prevent any electrical hazards.
rn
rn4. Mounting Instructions
rn- The device should be installed in a restricted access area, ensuring that it remains out of reach of the operator during normal operation.
rn- Secure the device firmly in its designated location to prevent any accidental displacement.
rn
rn5. Water Exposure
rn- Avoid exposing the device directly to water, as it is not built to withstand water exposure and may malfunction as a result.
rn
rn6. Installation Conditions
rn- Installation and handling of the device should not be performed during a lightning storm to avoid the risk of electrical shock or damage.

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Preventive Measures

rnrn

1. Interference and Placement
rn- All wireless data transmission devices, including the E-101, may cause interference that can affect other nearby electronic devices.
rn- Ensure that the device is placed in a location that minimizes potential interference with other equipment.
rn
rn2. Qualified Personnel
rn- Only qualified and trained personnel should handle the connection and installation of the device. This is to ensure both personal safety and the integrity of the device.
rn
rn3. Firm Installation
rn- The device must be securely fastened in its predetermined location to prevent any movement that could disrupt its operation or cause damage.
rn
rn4. Programming & Power Supply
rn- Perform any programming tasks using a PC that has an independent power supply. This prevents any risk associated with power fluctuations or failures during the programming process.
rn
rn5. Water & Humidity
rn-The E-101 device is sensitive to water and humidity. Take measures to protect it from these elements to avoid internal damage.
rn
rn6. Maintain Device Cleanliness
rn- Keep the device clean and free from dust and debris to maintain optimal performance.
rn
rn7. Regular Inspection
rn- Regularly inspect the device and its connections to ensure they remain secure and in good condition.

rn

title: SMS/GPRS Command Overview
discription:
The E-101 device is a versatile communication tool designed to receive commands via GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) and SMS (Short Message Service). GPRS enables the device to maintain a continuous internet connection for real-time data transmission and command reception, making it ideal for remote monitoring and control applications. SMS provides a reliable alternative for sending commands when GPRS connectivity is unavailable or limited. All commands are case sensitive.
nDifference between SMS & GPRS Commands is that SMS commands do not make use of the internet service and are sent using SMS recharges, but GPRS command are sent using Internet data. Another difference lies in their syntax/architecture. But their working & flow of execution of task is as same as SMS commands’. Clients can make use of the FOTAWEB platform which is an additional feature provided by the company for easy and fast configuration of devices on which these GPRS commands can be sent.

title: Vehicle Installation
discription:
1.  Selection of installation spot

rnrn

The ADAS should be installed at the top of the front windshield. In order to avoid affecting the driver's sight, it is better to install it above the right co-pilot seat and as close as possible to the center line of the vehicle.
rnThe equipment has a built-in GPS positioning antenna. In order to avoid interference, the equipment should try to avoid the black shading area at the middle and upper part of the front windshield.

rnrn

2.After the installation position is selected, paste the main engine on the selected position. Before fixing, please wipe the windshield clean, which can be wiped with adhesive. When pasting, ensure the horizontal angle of the main engine, and the left and right sides cannot be tilted. The main engine needs to be pressed for more than 1 minute to ensure the bonding strength, and the wiring harness of the main engine is hidden in the lining plate of the roof.

rnrn

3. Run the main-unit cable across the headliner and down to the driver side under-dash. This may require removing the A-pillar temporarily. Follow factory harnesses, always run behind any airbags.

title: ADAS Callibration
discription:
1. Body parameter measurement

rnrn

Measure the required vehicle parameters: car body width, the distance from the center of ADAS camera to the left side of the vehicle, the installation height of the camera (the height of the center of ADAS camera perpendicular to the ground) and the distance from ADAS camera to the front bumper of the vehicle, and record the test results. Later, enter the corresponding body parameters in the calibration of the Atlanta Tool V3.8.5 app “ADAS".

rnrn

2. Parameter setting before calibration

rnrn

After the mobile phone is connected to the ADAS Hostpot, open the Atlanta Tool V3.8.5 app, log in and enter the interface, click “All” button in the lower right corner, and select the ADAS button under "Calibration" in the menu bar to enter the ADAS calibration interface.

rnrn

rnrn

Before calibration, you need to set the parameters of the vehicle, and the following parameters must be filled in correctly. Click "Start Calibration" after filling in. The specific instructions are as follows:

rnrn

rnrn

Vehicle width: the actual width of the vehicle.

rnrn

Camera to left side of vehicle: distance from center of ADAS camera to left side.

rnrn

Camera installation height: the vertical distance between the center of ADAS camera and the ground.

rnrn

Camera to bumper: Measure the distance from the ADAS camera to the front of the car, which is generally 0.

rnrn

Note: These entries are for representational purposes only. Actual measurements may vary depending upon your vehicle.

rnrn

3. Horizon calibration

rnrn

Park the vehicle on a flat road to ensure a wide field of vision in front of it, adjust the angle of the camera so that the distant skyline (the junction of heaven and earth) in the video coincides with the horizontal center line in the app (the horizontal green dotted line) (if it can't completely coincide, you can fine-tune it by using the up and down arrow keys), and then click to finish the calibration.

rnrn

rnrn

4. Calibration rod calibration

rnrn

Place a calibration rod at the position in front of the car (in front of the camera) (the distance L between points A and B must be more than 2m), and the height h2 of the calibration rod must be the same as the height h1 of the center point of the ADAS lens from the ground, as shown in the following figure:

title: Installation Guidelines
discription:
1. Connecting Wires

rnrn

- Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.
rn- Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.
rn- Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.
rn- Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source

rnrn

- Power Retention During Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.
rn- Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.
rn- Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and rotection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire

rnrn

- Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.
rn- Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.
rn- Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire

rnrn

- Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.
rn- Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.
rn- Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

*RELAY DIAGRAM*

rnrn

 

rnrn

Relay Wiring Diagram Explanation

rnrn

To properly connect the relay for your device, follow these detailed instructions:
rn1. Pin 85
rnConnect the wire on pin 85 pin with the power source. Ensure that the power supply voltage matches the voltage requirements of your vehicle.
rn
rn2. Pin 87A (Normally Closed) and Pin 30 (Common Connection)
rn- Pin 30: You need to cut the vehicle’s ignition wire and connect one end to Pin 87A and connect ignition sense wire of the device.
rn- Pin 87A: Connect it to the ACC (Accessory), Vehicles/ Key Switch wire of your vehicle.
rn
rn3. Pin 86
rnConnect this pin to the device's ignition control wire. This wire controls the relay’s switching based on the ignition status.
rn
rnBy following these connections, you ensure that the relay is correctly wired to manage the ignition and power supply for your device, allowing for proper operation and control.

rnrn

 

rnrn

NOTE: Power Supply Connection Guidelines

rnrn

Optimal Connection Point
rnWhen connecting the power supply for the EL-100 device, it is crucial to select a point with very low impedance on the vehicle's onboard network. Such points are typically found at the battery terminals of the car. This ensures stable voltage supply and minimizes the risk of electrical interference.
rn
rnRecommended Connection Methods
rn1. Direct Battery Terminal Connection: It is highly recommended to connect the EL-100's power wires (GND and POWER) directly to the battery terminals. This direct connection provides a reliable and stable power source for the device.
rn2. Fuse Box Connection: Alternatively, you can connect the wires to the main POWER cable inside the vehicle's fuse box. Ensure that the fuse box is connected to the vehicle's computer power supply. This method also provides a controlled power supply environment.
rn
rnGround Connection Considerations
rn- GND Wire Connection: The GND wire must be connected to a designated point specifically designed for connecting vehicle computer grounds. Avoid arbitrary grounding to the car's mass, as this can introduce unpredictable static and dynamic potentials, potentially leading to unstable operation or failure of the EL-100 device.
rn
rnBy adhering to these detailed connection guidelines, you can ensure the proper and reliable operation of the EL-100 device within your vehicle's electrical system. Always prioritize stable connections and avoid any practices that could compromise the device's performance or safety.

rn

title: Safety Instructions
discription:
Operating the EL-100 device safely requires careful attention to the following guidelines and recommendations. Adhering to these instructions will help you avoid hazardous situations and ensure the optimal performance of your device. Please read and follow these instructions meticulously before operating the device.

rnrn

A. Safety instructions

rnrn

1. Power Specifications
rn- The EL-100 device operates on a nominal voltage of +12 VDC/+24 VDC/+48 VDC/+74 VDC.
rn- The allowable voltage range for safe operation is between +9 V DC and +90 V DC.

rnrn


rn2. Transportation and Handling
rn- To prevent mechanical damage during transportation, ensure that the device is packaged in an impact-resistant container.
rn- When setting up the device, place it in a location where the LED indicators are clearly visible. These indicators provide essential information about the device's operational status.
rn
rn3. Connection and Disconnection Procedures
rn- When connecting the wiring cables to the vehicle, make sure to disconnect the relevant jumpers from the vehicle's power supply first.
rn- Before removing the device from the vehicle, always disconnect the wiring harness connection to prevent any electrical hazards.
rn
rn4. Mounting Instructions
rn- The device should be installed in a restricted access area, ensuring that it remains out of reach of the operator during normal operation.
rn- Secure the device firmly in its designated location to prevent any accidental displacement.
rn- The device should be installed with a sky view and kept away from metal surfaces.
rn
rn5. Water Exposure
rn- Avoid exposing the device directly to water, as it is not built to withstand water exposure and may malfunction as a result.
rn
rn6. Installation Conditions
rn- Installation and handling of the device should not be performed during a lightning storm to avoid the risk of electrical shock or damage.

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Preventive Measures

rnrn

1. Interference and Placement
rn- All wireless data transmission devices, including the EL-100, may cause interference that can affect other nearby electronic devices.
rn- Ensure that the device is placed in a location that minimizes potential interference with other equipment.
rn
rn2. Qualified Personnel
rn- Only qualified and trained personnel should handle the connection and installation of the device. This is to ensure both personal safety and the integrity of the device.
rn
rn3. Firm Installation
rn- The device must be securely fastened in its predetermined location to prevent any movement that could disrupt its operation or cause damage.
rn
rn4. Programming & Power Supply
rn- Perform any programming tasks using a PC that has an independent power supply. This prevents any risk associated with power fluctuations or failures during the programming process.
rn
rn5. Water & Humidity
rn-The EL-100 device is sensitive to water and humidity. Take measures to protect it from these elements to avoid internal damage.
rn
rn6. Maintain Device Cleanliness
rn- Keep the device clean and free from dust and debris to maintain optimal performance.
rn
rn7. Regular Inspection
rn- Regularly inspect the device and its connections to ensure they remain secure and in good condition.

rn

title: SMS/GPRS Command Overview
discription:
The EL-100 device is a versatile communication tool designed to receive commands via GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) and SMS (Short Message Service). GPRS enables the device to maintain a continuous internet connection for real-time data transmission and command reception, making it ideal for remote monitoring and control applications. SMS provides a reliable alternative for sending commands when GPRS connectivity is unavailable or limited.

rnrn

All commands are case sensitive.  

rnrn

While SMS commands are sent using recharges, GPRS commands are sent via internet. Another difference lies in their syntax. But their working & flow of execution of task is same. title: Main Unit Preparation Installation
discription:
The main unit comes prepared for bus/large truck setup or small vehicles

rnrn

Unit Preparation for Installation

rnrn

1. Open the front cover plate of the MDVR using the specialized key.

rnrn

2. By unscrewing the screws, remove the hard disk support plate and insert the desired storage device, be it Hard disk drive (HDD) or SD card in the designated place.

rnrn

3. Insert the SIM card and memory card (If needed). Please pay attention to the chip direction.

rnrn

4. Insert back the support plate and screw it back.

rnrn

5. Lock the front cover plate using the key.

rnrn

Note:

rnrn

1. Point number 5 is compulsory because it is mandatory to properly lock the front cover plate for the MDVR to start recording. If this lock is left in the unlock position, recording can’t be started, and video recording will be saved.

rnrn

2. Please use the appropriate key for opening & closing the front cover plate and the plastic cover.

rnrn

3. For Storage Drivers: Please use SanDisk, Kingston, or customized SD Card, Hard disk drives (HDD) or Solid State Drives (SSD) purchased through regular channels.

rnrn

After installing all accessories, close the plastic cover and lock it with a specialized key.

rnrn

title: Vehicle Installation
discription:
1.  Selection of installation spot -

rnrn

Installation spot varies invariably. When there is a cabin available the MDVR is then attached there, In case a cabin is not available then MDVR is either screwed under the dashboard or above the dashboard. Sometimes the MDVR is also attached behind the driver. Another place where MDVR can be screwed is a place where baggage is put above the seats. Sometimes driver also says to put the device under his seat. One advice for placing the MDVR is always to select a position where there good support can be provided.

rnrn

2. After the installation position is selected, then tighten the MDVR at the selected spot either with screws or with 3m double-sided strong adhesive tape. Before fixing with tape, please wipe the surface clean, which can be wiped with adhesive. The MDVR needs to be pressed for more than 1 minute to ensure the bonding strength and the wiring harness is hidden in the lining plate of the roof.

rnrn

3. Try to keep the harness of the MDVR hidden to avoid any short-circuit due to cutting or any so reasons. There should be enough space and fire-resistant pipes on the external cables of the device to avoid electric leakage caused by abrasion and aging.

rnrn

4. Attach the antennas to the back of the device in their designated places (LTE/GNSS/WiFi). You can get these antennas in the box containing the MDVR itself.

title: Main Engine Power Supply Connection & LED Indication
meta_description: Main Engine Power Supply Connection & LED Indication
discription:
You are required to use the in-box containing power and AV1-AV4 cable. Before connecting, please check the power supply voltage, which should be within the range of 8-36V. The recommended working voltage is 12v or 24v. When the length of the power cord is not enough, extra wire can be used to extend the wiring.

rnrn

The red wire of the power cable is connected to the positive pole of the battery, black wires (2) to the negative pole & yellow wire to the Ignition point to sense the ignition of the vehicle (only in case when MDVR is suited to be turned on when the vehicle moves), but for continuous recording combine the red and yellow for connection to the positive pole of the battery.

rnrn

When connecting the power adapter to debug the equipment, please connect the red wire and the yellow wire to the positive pole of the power supply.

rnrn

 

rnrn

LED Indication

rnrn

When the equipment is normally powered on, the PWR indicator light will turn green, which is always on. When the equipment is started normally, the green indicator light will flash once it senses the recording in the storage device be it HDD, SSD, or SD Card

title: Quick SMS Configuration
discription:
The default configuration ensures optimal track quality and efficient data usage. Follow these steps to quickly set up your device via SMS commands.

rnrn

A. Commands to Change Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To port the device to a SERVER
rn- Command: #SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;<password>
rn- Example: #SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000; <6906>
rn- Description: This command directs the EL-400 device to connect to the server specified by the given IP address and port number. In the example, the device will be configured to communicate with the server at IP 196.168.175.12 and port 20000.

rnrn

2. To change the APN settings
rn- Command: #CONFIG::APN::username::password;<password>
rn- Purpose: Configures your GPRS account settings.
rn- Details:

rnrn

- APN (Access Point Name): Used to access the GPRS gateway provided by your network operator.
rn- Username: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).
rn- Password: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).
rn- Example: For the Idea network without internet, the command would be: #CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>

rnrn

3. PPI Configuration
rn- Command: WEBSTART<xxx/H/M/S>,<yyy/H/M/S><zzz/H/M/S><z1z1z1/H/M/S><password>
rn- Purpose: Command to set the tracking interval and you will get confirmation SMS and then start sending data to our web server, where xxx stands for active(IGN ON) interval, yyy stands for passive(IGN OFF) interval, zzz stands for Main Power Removal interval and z1z1z1 stands for panic interval. H - Hours, M-Minutes, S- Seconds
rn- Example: WEBSTART030S,030S,030S,030S<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Commands to Check Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Check the GPRS Status
rn- Command: GPRSSTATUS<6906>
rn- Purpose: Retrieves the complete status of the device.

rnrn

Description of the reply is as follows:

2. To Get GPS Details

rnrn

Send the command `GETGPS<password>` to the EL-400 device.

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are unreachable: You will receive the message "GPS NOT FOUND."
rn- If GPS satellites are reachable: You will receive a web link to view the location on a map.

rnrn

Additionally, you will receive the following information:
rn- Speed: Indicates the speed of the vehicle in KPH.
rn- Date: The date of the recorded data.
rn- Time: The time of the recorded data in IST.

rnrn

To view the exact location on Google Maps, enter the latitude and longitude coordinates separated by a comma (,) in the search bar at [www.maps.google.com](http://www.maps.google.com). This will show the precise location on the map.

rnrn

3.To Check the Status of the System
rnCommand: SYSSTATUS<6906>

rn- Main power status
rn- Ignition status
rn- Immobilizer status
rn- PANIC status
rn- No Meaning
rn- Reserved field
rn- Odometer (KM)
rn- Onboard temperature
rn- Internal battery voltage
rn- O/P2 Status

rnrn

D. FR<6906>:

rnrn

This Command is used to set factory default values. After this, all the user configured settings will be erased and factory fitted values will be implemented.

rnrn

 

rnrn

E. Default Configuration Settings

rnrn

1. Movement and Ignition Detection

rnrn

- Movement Detection: The device detects vehicle movement using the accelerometer.
rn- Ignition Detection: The ignition is detected by the vehicle's power voltage, which should range between 8 and 90 volts.

rnrn

2. Device Recording on Movement
rn- Recording Conditions: When the vehicle covers a distance of at least 50 meters while in idle mode, the device will begin tracking the movement of the vehicle.
rn- Stop Detection: The device will mark the vehicle as stopped if it remains stationary for one continuous minute.

rnrn

3. Device Recording on Stop
rn- Recording Conditions: If the vehicle remains stationary for one continuous minute, the device will mark it as stopped.(Speed 0kmph and no signal from motion sensors/accelerometer)

rnrn

4. Sending Records to Server
rn- Data Transmission: Once a record is made, it is sent to the server according to the default settings. Data can be sent based on specific criteria such as set time intervals, alerts, angle changes, and distance traveled.

rnrn

5. Synchronization and Updates
rnAfter a successful SMS configuration, the EL-400 device will synchronize its time and update the records to the configured server. Users can modify time intervals and default I/O elements using the Atlanta Configurator tool or additional SMS commands. This ensures that the device remains accurate and up-to-date, providing reliable data for monitoring vehicle movement and status.

rn

title: Installation Guidelines
discription:
1. Connecting Wires

rnrn

- Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.
rn- Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.
rn- Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.
rn- Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source

rnrn

- Power Retention During Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.
rn- Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.
rn- Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and rotection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire

rnrn

- Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.
rn- Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.
rn- Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire

rnrn

- Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.
rn- Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.
rn- Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

*RELAY DIAGRAM*

rnrn

 

rnrn

Relay Wiring Diagram Explanation

rnrn

To properly connect the relay for your device, follow these detailed instructions:
rn1. Pin 85
rnConnect the wire on pin 85 pin with the power source. Ensure that the power supply voltage matches the voltage requirements of your vehicle.
rn
rn2. Pin 87A (Normally Closed) and Pin 30 (Common Connection)
rn- Pin 30: You need to cut the vehicle’s ignition wire and connect one end to Pin 87A and connect ignition sense wire of the device.
rn- Pin 87A: Connect it to the ACC (Accessory), Vehicles/ Key Switch wire of your vehicle.
rn
rn3. Pin 86
rnConnect this pin to the device's ignition control wire. This wire controls the relay’s switching based on the ignition status.
rn
rnBy following these connections, you ensure that the relay is correctly wired to manage the ignition and power supply for your device, allowing for proper operation and control.

rnrn

 

rnrn

NOTE: Power Supply Connection Guidelines

rnrn

Optimal Connection Point
rnWhen connecting the power supply for the EL-400 device, it is crucial to select a point with very low impedance on the vehicle's onboard network. Such points are typically found at the battery terminals of the car. This ensures stable voltage supply and minimizes the risk of electrical interference.
rn
rnRecommended Connection Methods
rn1. Direct Battery Terminal Connection: It is highly recommended to connect the EL-400's power wires (GND and POWER) directly to the battery terminals. This direct connection provides a reliable and stable power source for the device.
rn2. Fuse Box Connection: Alternatively, you can connect the wires to the main POWER cable inside the vehicle's fuse box. Ensure that the fuse box is connected to the vehicle's computer power supply. This method also provides a controlled power supply environment.
rn
rnGround Connection Considerations
rn- GND Wire Connection: The GND wire must be connected to a designated point specifically designed for connecting vehicle computer grounds. Avoid arbitrary grounding to the car's mass, as this can introduce unpredictable static and dynamic potentials, potentially leading to unstable operation or failure of the EL-400 device.
rn
rnBy adhering to these detailed connection guidelines, you can ensure the proper and reliable operation of the EL-400 device within your vehicle's electrical system. Always prioritize stable connections and avoid any practices that could compromise the device's performance or safety.

title: Safety Instructions
discription:
Operating the EL-400 device safely requires careful attention to the following guidelines and recommendations. Adhering to these instructions will help you avoid hazardous situations and ensure the optimal performance of your device. Please read and follow these instructions meticulously before operating the device.

rnrn

A. Safety instructions

rnrn

1. Power Specifications
rn- The EL-400 device operates on a nominal voltage of +12 VDC/+24 VDC/+48 VDC/+74 VDC.
rn- The allowable voltage range for safe operation is between +9 V DC and +90 V DC.

rnrn


rn2. Transportation and Handling
rn- To prevent mechanical damage during transportation, ensure that the device is packaged in an impact-resistant container.
rn- When setting up the device, place it in a location where the LED indicators are clearly visible. These indicators provide essential information about the device's operational status.
rn
rn3. Connection and Disconnection Procedures
rn- When connecting the wiring cables to the vehicle, make sure to disconnect the relevant jumpers from the vehicle's power supply first.
rn- Before removing the device from the vehicle, always disconnect the wiring harness connection to prevent any electrical hazards.
rn
rn4. Mounting Instructions
rn- The device should be installed in a restricted access area, ensuring that it remains out of reach of the operator during normal operation.
rn- Secure the device firmly in its designated location to prevent any accidental displacement.
rn- The device should be installed with a sky view and kept away from metal surfaces.
rn
rn5. Water Exposure
rn- Avoid exposing the device directly to water, as it is not built to withstand water exposure and may malfunction as a result.
rn
rn6. Installation Conditions
rn- Installation and handling of the device should not be performed during a lightning storm to avoid the risk of electrical shock or damage.

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Preventive Measures

rnrn

1. Interference and Placement
rn- All wireless data transmission devices, including the EL-400, may cause interference that can affect other nearby electronic devices.
rn- Ensure that the device is placed in a location that minimizes potential interference with other equipment.
rn
rn2. Qualified Personnel
rn- Only qualified and trained personnel should handle the connection and installation of the device. This is to ensure both personal safety and the integrity of the device.
rn
rn3. Firm Installation
rn- The device must be securely fastened in its predetermined location to prevent any movement that could disrupt its operation or cause damage.
rn
rn4. Programming & Power Supply
rn- Perform any programming tasks using a PC that has an independent power supply. This prevents any risk associated with power fluctuations or failures during the programming process.
rn
rn5. Water & Humidity
rn-The EL-400 device is sensitive to water and humidity. Take measures to protect it from these elements to avoid internal damage.
rn
rn6. Maintain Device Cleanliness
rn- Keep the device clean and free from dust and debris to maintain optimal performance.
rn
rn7. Regular Inspection
rn- Regularly inspect the device and its connections to ensure they remain secure and in good condition.

rn

title: SMS/GPRS Command Overview
discription:
The EL-400 device is a versatile communication tool designed to receive commands via GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) and SMS (Short Message Service). GPRS enables the device to maintain a continuous internet connection for real-time data transmission and command reception, making it ideal for remote monitoring and control applications. SMS provides a reliable alternative for sending commands when GPRS connectivity is unavailable or limited.

rnrn

All commands are case sensitive.  

rnrn

While SMS commands are sent using recharges, GPRS commands are sent via internet. Another difference lies in their syntax. But their working & flow of execution of task is same. Clients can make use of the FOTAWEB platform which is an additional feature provided by the company for easy and fast configuration of devices on which these GPRS commands can be sent.

title: Main Unit Preparation Installation
discription:
The main unit comes prepared for bus/large truck setup or small vehicles

rnrn

Unit Preparation for Installation

rnrn

1. Open the front cover plate of the MDVR using the specialized key.

rnrn

2. By unscrewing the screws, remove the hard disk support plate and insert the desired storage device, be it Hard disk drive (HDD) or SD card in the designated place.

rnrn

3. Insert the SIM card and memory card (If needed). Please pay attention to the chip direction.

rnrn

4. Insert back the support plate and screw it back.

rnrn

5. Lock the front cover plate using the key.

rnrn

Note:

rnrn

1. Point number 5 is compulsory because it is mandatory to properly lock the front cover plate for the MDVR to start recording. If this lock is left in the unlock position, recording can’t be started, and video recording will be saved.

rnrn

2. Please use the appropriate key for opening & closing the front cover plate and the plastic cover.

rnrn

3. For Storage Drivers: Please use SanDisk, Kingston, or customized SD Card, Hard disk drives (HDD) or Solid State Drives (SSD) purchased through regular channels.

rnrn

After installing all accessories, close the plastic cover and lock it with a specialized key.

rnrn

title: Vehicle Installation
discription:
1.  Selection of installation spot -

rnrn

Installation spot varies invariably. When there is a cabin available the MDVR is then attached there, In case a cabin is not available then MDVR is either screwed under the dashboard or above the dashboard. Sometimes the MDVR is also attached behind the driver. Another place where MDVR can be screwed is a place where baggage is put above the seats. Sometimes driver also says to put the device under his seat. One advice for placing the MDVR is always to select a position where good support can be provided.

rnrn

2. After the installation position is selected, then tighten the MDVR at the selected spot either with screws or with 3m double-sided strong adhesive tape. Before fixing with tape, please wipe the surface clean, which can be wiped with adhesive. The MDVR needs to be pressed for more than 1 minute to ensure the bonding strength and the wiring harness is hidden in the lining plate of the roof.

rnrn

3. Try to keep the harness of the MDVR hidden to avoid any short-circuit due to cutting or any so reasons. There should be enough space and fire-resistant pipes on the external cables of the device to avoid electric leakage caused by abrasion and aging.

rnrn

4. Attach the antennas to the back of the device in their designated places (LTE/GNSS/WiFi). You can get these antennas in the box containing the MDVR itself.

title: Main Engine Power Supply Connection & LED Indication
meta_description: Main Engine Power Supply Connection & LED Indication
discription:
You are required to use the in-box containing power and AV1-AV4 cable. Before connecting, please check the power supply voltage, which should be within the range of 8-36V. The recommended working voltage is 12v or 24v. When the length of the power cord is not enough, extra wire can be used to extend the wiring.

rnrn

The red wire of the power cable is connected to the positive pole of the battery, black wires (2) to the negative pole & yellow wire to the Ignition point to sense the ignition of the vehicle (only in case when MDVR is suited to be turned on when the vehicle moves), but for continuous recording combine the red and yellow for connection to the positive pole of the battery.

rnrn

When connecting the power adapter to debug the equipment, please connect the red wire and the yellow wire to the positive pole of the power supply.

rnrn

 

rnrn

LED Indication

rnrn

When the equipment is normally powered on, the PWR indicator light will turn green, which is always on. When the equipment is started normally, the green indicator light will flash once it senses the recording in the storage device be it HDD, SSD, or SD Card

title: HD-04G Configuration
discription:
First, you have to install the MDVR on the vehicle and then only the configuration can be done. Its configuration is done physically using a TFT Monitor display.

rnrn

The TFT can configure the MDVR in offline mode and you can configure various settings such as vehicle details, video recording settings of various cameras, Date & Time, and many other variables.

title: HD-04G Parameters Configuration Tool
discription:
You can configure the MDVR using the TFT in offline mode by physically connecting the MDVR and TFT via appropriate connectors. Let’s understand the various configuration parameters using the TFT Monitor Display.

rnrn

First, you have to connect the MDVR with the TFT using an appropriate connector. The connector of the TFT display is connected to the AVOUT cable of MDVR. Then a wired optical mouse is connected to the USB port of MDVR to easily use the TFT monitor display.

rnrn

NOTE: This configuration is common for all MDVR models, so some settings like 3G/4G, NetState, WiFi Settings, and Server Settings won’t work in this model because this just is used for offline recording. Ignore the settings that aren’t applicable in this model.

rnrn

 

rnrn

MDVR Configuration using TFT is as follows:

rnrn

First of all this user login page will pop up, then only you can proceed with the configuration.

rnrn

 

rnrn

User Login

rnrn

Right-click the mouse, Device will show the login interface, please input your UserName, Password, and select your language, click “OK” to login to the menu.  (The default UserName is admin, without Password/ use 123456 as password), as shown below:

rnrn

rnrn

 

rnrn

Path: Basic->DateTime, see as follows:

rnrn

rnrn

TimeSYNC: Date and Time can be synchronized with GPS/BD

rnrn

 

rnrn

4. Set up cameras

rnrn

Path: Menu->Record->Mode. Please set up your cameras’ SignalType, Valid/Invalid. The DVR works with both AHD and general cameras. If you use AHD cameras, please select the first Type, if you use general cameras, please select the third Type, if you use both of general and AHD cameras, please select the second Type. See as following:

rnrn

  

rnrn

 

rnrn

5. Wizard

rnrn

Path: Menu->Wizard. This Wizard will help you to quickly set up the device to connect with the server.

rnrn

5.1 Vehicle Information Setup

rnrn

rnrn

The DVR is using “Device ID” to connect with the server, so please input the correct DeviceID which was registered on the server for your device. The user can modify the VehicleName and PlateNumber according to their requirement. The PlateNumber is the vehicle’s plate number, and it will be displayed in the video.

rnrn

5.2 Disk Management

rnrn

Disk needs to be formatted in the device when using it for the first time. If the disk was not detected by the device, please check the disk lock and make sure it is well-locked

rnrn

The device will detect the 3G/4G Module Type automatically. Please insert the right SIM card that corresponds with the Module Type detected. Please consult your SIM card carrier or search on the internet to make sure you put the correct parameters (Dial Number, APN, Username, and Password). If you use a VPN, please consult your telecom carrier to get the correct parameters.

rnrn

The days in yellow are with recorded video. The blue parts in the timeline bar are with recorded video. Please move the cursor of your mouse at the corresponding channel and time, and then left-click it to replay the video.

The On/Off “Volt” setting is for setting the voltage to shut down and start on the device, this feature can prevent the device drained the vehicle’s battery.

rnrn

The device will detect the current-voltage automatically, when the vehicle’s battery voltage is lower than the Shut Volt, the device will shut down automatically to avoid draining the battery. When the voltage is higher than the Power Volt, the device can be started on.

title: Main Unit Preparation Installation
discription:
The main unit comes prepared for bus/large truck setup or small vehicles

rnrn

Unit Preparation for Installation

rnrn

1. Open the front cover plate of the MDVR using the specialized key.

rnrn

2. By unscrewing the screws, remove the hard disk support plate and insert the desired storage device, be it Hard disk drive (HDD) or SD card in the designated place.

rnrn

3. Insert the SIM card and memory card (If needed). Please pay attention to the chip direction.

rnrn

4. Insert back the support plate and screw it back.

rnrn

5. Lock the front cover plate using the key.

rnrn

Note:

rnrn

1. Point number 5 is compulsory because it is mandatory to properly lock the front cover plate for the MDVR to start recording. If this lock is left in the unlock position, recording can’t be started, and video recording will be saved.

rnrn

2. Please use the appropriate key for opening & closing the front cover plate and the plastic cover.

rnrn

3. For Storage Drivers: Please use SanDisk, Kingston, or customized SD Card, Hard disk drives (HDD) or Solid State Drives (SSD) purchased through regular channels.

rnrn

After installing all accessories, close the plastic cover and lock it with a specialized key.

rnrn

title: HD-04GG Vehicle Installation
discription:
1.  Selection of installation spot -

rnrn

Installation spot varies invariably. When there is a cabin available the MDVR is then attached there, In case a cabin is not available then MDVR is either screwed under the dashboard or above the dashboard. Sometimes the MDVR is also attached behind the driver. Another place where MDVR can be screwed is a place where baggage is put above the seats. Sometimes driver also says to put the device under his seat. One advice for placing the MDVR is always to select a position where there good support can be provided.

rnrn

2. After the installation position is selected, then tighten the MDVR at the selected spot either with screws or with 3m double-sided strong adhesive tape. Before fixing with tape, please wipe the surface clean, which can be wiped with adhesive. The MDVR needs to be pressed for more than 1 minute to ensure the bonding strength and the wiring harness is hidden in the lining plate of the roof.

rnrn

3. Try to keep the harness of the MDVR hidden to avoid any short-circuit due to cutting or any so reasons. There should be enough space and fire-resistant pipes on the external cables of the device to avoid electric leakage caused by abrasion and aging.

rnrn

4. Attach the antennas to the back of the device in their designated places (LTE/GNSS/WiFi). You can get these antennas in the box containing the MDVR itself.

title: Main Engine Power Supply Connection & LED Indication
meta_description: Main Engine Power Supply Connection & LED Indication
discription:
You are required to use the in-box containing power and AV1-AV4 cable. Before connecting, please check the power supply voltage, which should be within the range of 8-36V. The recommended working voltage is 12v or 24v. When the length of the power cord is not enough, extra wire can be used to extend the wiring.

rnrn

The red wire of the power cable is connected to the positive pole of the battery, black wires (2) to the negative pole & yellow wire to the Ignition point to sense the ignition of the vehicle (only in case when MDVR is suited to be turned on when the vehicle moves), but for continuous recording combine the red and yellow for connection to the positive pole of the battery.

rnrn

When connecting the power adapter to debug the equipment, please connect the red wire and the yellow wire to the positive pole of the power supply.

rnrn

 

rnrn

LED Indication

rnrn

When the equipment is normally powered on, the PWR indicator light will turn green, which is always on. When the equipment is started normally, the green indicator light will flash once it senses the recording in the storage device be it HDD, SSD, or SD Card

The on/Off “Ctrl” setting is for starting on and shutting down the device automatically WHEN THE DEVICE IS ON STANDBY AFTER ACC IGNITION OFF. You can set up three-time segments.

rnrn

rnrn

The On/Off “Volt” setting is for setting the voltage to shut down and start on the device, this feature can prevent the device drained the vehicle’s battery.

rnrn

The device will detect the current-voltage automatically, when the vehicle’s battery voltage is lower than the Shut Volt, the device will shut down automatically to avoid draining the battery. When the voltage is higher than the Power Volt, the device can be started on.

title: Main Unit Preparation Installation
discription:
The main unit comes prepared for bus/large truck setup or small vehicles

rnrn

Unit Preparation for Installation

rnrn

1. Open the front cover plate of the MDVR using the specialized key.

rnrn

2. By unscrewing the screws, remove the hard disk support plate and insert the desired storage device, be it Hard disk drive (HDD) or SD card in the designated place.

rnrn

3. Insert the SIM card and memory card (If needed). Please pay attention to the chip direction.

rnrn

4. Insert back the support plate and screw it back.

rnrn

5. Lock the front cover plate using the key.

rnrn

Note:

rnrn

1. Point number 5 is compulsory because it is mandatory to properly lock the front cover plate for the MDVR to start recording. If this lock is left in the unlock position, recording can’t be started, and video recording will be saved.

rnrn

2. Please use the appropriate key for opening & closing the front cover plate and the plastic cover.

rnrn

3. For Storage Drivers: Please use SanDisk, Kingston, or customized SD Card, Hard disk drives (HDD) or Solid State Drives (SSD) purchased through regular channels.

rnrn

After installing all accessories, close the plastic cover and lock it with a specialized key.

rnrn

title: Vehicle Installation
discription:
1.  Selection of installation spot -

rnrn

Installation spot varies invariably. When there is a cabin available the MDVR is then attached there, In case a cabin is not available then MDVR is either screwed under the dashboard or above the dashboard. Sometimes the MDVR is also attached behind the driver. Another place where MDVR can be screwed is a place where baggage is put above the seats. Sometimes driver also says to put the device under his seat. One advice for placing the MDVR is always to select a position where there good support can be provided.

rnrn

2. After the installation position is selected, then tighten the MDVR at the selected spot either with screws or with 3m double-sided strong adhesive tape. Before fixing with tape, please wipe the surface clean, which can be wiped with adhesive. The MDVR needs to be pressed for more than 1 minute to ensure the bonding strength and the wiring harness is hidden in the lining plate of the roof.

rnrn

3. Try to keep the harness of the MDVR hidden to avoid any short-circuit due to cutting or any so reasons. There should be enough space and fire-resistant pipes on the external cables of the device to avoid electric leakage caused by abrasion and aging.

rnrn

4. Attach the antennas to the back of the device in their designated places (LTE/GNSS/WiFi). You can get these antennas in the box containing the MDVR itself.

title: Main Engine Power Supply Connection & LED Indication
meta_description: Main Engine Power Supply Connection & LED Indication
discription:
You are required to use the in-box containing power and AV1-AV4 cable. Before connecting, please check the power supply voltage, which should be within the range of 8-36V. The recommended working voltage is 12v or 24v. When the length of the power cord is not enough, extra wire can be used to extend the wiring.

rnrn

The red wire of the power cable is connected to the positive pole of the battery, black wires (2) to the negative pole & yellow wire to the Ignition point to sense the ignition of the vehicle (only in case when MDVR is suited to be turned on when the vehicle moves), but for continuous recording combine the red and yellow for connection to the positive pole of the battery.

rnrn

When connecting the power adapter to debug the equipment, please connect the red wire and the yellow wire to the positive pole of the power supply.

rnrn

 

rnrn

LED Indication

rnrn

When the equipment is normally powered on, the PWR indicator light will turn green, which is always on. When the equipment is started normally, the green indicator light will flash once it senses the recording in the storage device be it HDD, SSD, or SD Card

title: Quick SMS Configuration
discription:
The default configuration ensures optimal track quality and efficient data usage. Follow these steps to quickly set up your device via SMS commands.

rnrn

A. Commands to Change Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To port the device to a SERVER
rn- Command: #SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;<password>
rn- Example: #SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000;<6906>
rn- Description: This command directs the G-100 device to connect to the server specified by the given IP address and port number. In the example, the device will be configured to communicate with the server at IP 196.168.175.12 and port 20000.

rnrn

2. To change the APN settings
rn- Command: #CONFIG::APN::username::password;<password>
rn- Purpose: Configures your GPRS account settings.
rn- Details:

rnrn

- APN (Access Point Name): Used to access the GPRS gateway provided by your network operator.
rn- Username: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).
rn- Password: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).
rn- Example: For the Idea network without internet, the command would be: #CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>

rnrn

3. PPI Configuration
rn- Command: WEBSTART<xxx/H/M/S>,<yyy/H/M/S>,<zzz/H/M/S><password>
rn- Purpose: Start live tracking with different intervals depending on IGNITION ON ,IGNITION OFF & PANIC interval respectively . H - Hours, M-Minutes, S- Seconds
rn- Example: WEBSTART030S,002M,005S<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Commands to Check Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Check the GPRS Status
rn- Command: GPRSSTATUS<6906>
rn- Purpose: Retrieves the complete status of the device.

rnrn

Description of the reply is as follows:

rnrn

2. To Get GPS Details

rnrn

Send the command `GETGPS<password>` to the G-100 device.

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are unreachable: You will receive the message "GPS NOT FOUND."
rn- If GPS satellites are reachable: You will receive a web link to view the location on a map.

rnrn

Additionally, you will receive the following information:
rn- Speed: Indicates the speed of the vehicle in KPH.
rn- Date: The date of the recorded data.
rn- Time: The time of the recorded data in IST.

rnrn

To view the exact location on Google Maps, enter the latitude and longitude coordinates separated by a comma (,) in the search bar at [www.maps.google.com](http://www.maps.google.com). This will show the precise location on the map.

rnrn

3.To Check the Status of the System
rnCommand: SYSSTATUS<6906>
rnResponse: This command provides important system statuses, including:
rn- Main power status
rn- Ignition status
rn- Immobilizer status
rn- A/C status
rn- Door status
rn- Reserved low sense input
rn- Odometer (KM)
rn- Onboard temperature
rn- Internal battery voltage

rnrn

 

rnrn

C. FE<6906>: 

rnrn

This Command is used to clear the unsent memory data from flash.

rnrn

 

rnrn

D. FR<6906>:

rnrn

This Command is used to set factory default values. After this, all the user configured settings will be erased and factory fitted values will be implemented.

rnrn

 

rnrn

E. Default Configuration Settings

rnrn

1. Movement and Ignition Detection

rnrn

- Movement Detection: The device detects vehicle movement using the accelerometer.
rn- Ignition Detection: The ignition is detected by the vehicle's power voltage, which should range between 8 and 36 volts.

rnrn

2. Device Recording on Movement
rn- Recording Conditions: When the vehicle covers a distance of at least 50 meters while in idle mode, the device will begin tracking the movement of the vehicle.
rn- Stop Detection: The device will mark the vehicle as stopped if it remains stationary for one continuous minute.

rnrn

3. Device Recording on Stop
rn- Recording Conditions: If the vehicle remains stationary for one continuous minute, the device will mark it as stopped.(Speed 0kmph and no signal from motion sensors/accelerometer)

rnrn

4. Sending Records to Server
rn- Data Transmission: Once a record is made, it is sent to the server according to the default settings. Data can be sent based on specific criteria such as set time intervals, alerts, angle changes, and distance traveled.

rnrn

5. Synchronization and Updates
rnAfter a successful SMS configuration, the G-100 device will synchronize its time and update the records to the configured server. Users can modify time intervals and default I/O elements using the Atlanta Configurator tool or additional SMS commands. This ensures that the device remains accurate and up-to-date, providing reliable data for monitoring vehicle movement and status.

title: Installation Guidelines
discription:
1. Connecting Wires

rnrn

- Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.
rn- Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.
rn- Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.
rn- Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source

rnrn

- Power Retention During Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.
rn- Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.
rn- Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and rotection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire

rnrn

- Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.
rn- Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.
rn- Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire

rnrn

- Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.
rn- Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.
rn- Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

*RELAY DIAGRAM*

rnrn

 

rnrn

Relay Wiring Diagram Explanation

rnrn

To properly connect the relay for your device, follow these detailed instructions:
rn1. Pin 85
rnConnect the wire on pin 85 pin with the power source. Ensure that the power supply voltage matches the voltage requirements of your vehicle.
rn
rn2. Pin 87A (Normally Closed) and Pin 30 (Common Connection)
rn- Pin 30: You need to cut the vehicle’s ignition wire and connect one end to Pin 87A and connect ignition sense wire of the device.
rn- Pin 87A: Connect it to the ACC (Accessory), Vehicles/ Key Switch wire of your vehicle.
rn
rn3. Pin 86
rnConnect this pin to the device's ignition control wire. This wire controls the relay’s switching based on the ignition status.
rn
rnBy following these connections, you ensure that the relay is correctly wired to manage the ignition and power supply for your device, allowing for proper operation and control.

rnrn

 

rnrn

NOTE: Power Supply Connection Guidelines

rnrn

Optimal Connection Point
rnWhen connecting the power supply for the G-100 device, it is crucial to select a point with very low impedance on the vehicle's onboard network. Such points are typically found at the battery terminals of the car. This ensures stable voltage supply and minimizes the risk of electrical interference.
rn
rnRecommended Connection Methods
rn1. Direct Battery Terminal Connection: It is highly recommended to connect the G-100's power wires (GND and POWER) directly to the battery terminals. This direct connection provides a reliable and stable power source for the device.
rn2. Fuse Box Connection: Alternatively, you can connect the wires to the main POWER cable inside the vehicle's fuse box. Ensure that the fuse box is connected to the vehicle's computer power supply. This method also provides a controlled power supply environment.
rn
rnGround Connection Considerations
rn- GND Wire Connection: The GND wire must be connected to a designated point specifically designed for connecting vehicle computer grounds. Avoid arbitrary grounding to the car's mass, as this can introduce unpredictable static and dynamic potentials, potentially leading to unstable operation or failure of the G-100 device.
rn
rnBy adhering to these detailed connection guidelines, you can ensure the proper and reliable operation of the G-100 device within your vehicle's electrical system. Always prioritize stable connections and avoid any practices that could compromise the device's performance or safety.

title: Safety Instructions
discription:
Operating the G-100 device safely requires careful attention to the following guidelines and recommendations. Adhering to these instructions will help you avoid hazardous situations and ensure the optimal performance of your device. Please read and follow these instructions meticulously before operating the device.

rnrn

A. Safety instructions

rnrn

1. Power Specifications
rn- The G-100 device operates on a nominal voltage of +12 VDC/+24 VDC.
rn- The allowable voltage range for safe operation is between +8 V DC and +36 V DC.

rnrn


rn2. Transportation and Handling
rn- To prevent mechanical damage during transportation, ensure that the device is packaged in an impact-resistant container.
rn- When setting up the device, place it in a location where the LED indicators are clearly visible. These indicators provide essential information about the device's operational status.
rn
rn3. Connection and Disconnection Procedures
rn- When connecting the wiring cables to the vehicle, make sure to disconnect the relevant jumpers from the vehicle's power supply first.
rn- Before removing the device from the vehicle, always disconnect the wiring harness connection to prevent any electrical hazards.
rn
rn4. Mounting Instructions
rn- The device should be installed in a restricted access area, ensuring that it remains out of reach of the operator during normal operation.
rn- Secure the device firmly in its designated location to prevent any accidental displacement.
rn- The device should be installed with a sky view and kept away from metal surfaces.
rn
rn5. Water Exposure
rn- Avoid exposing the device directly to water, as it is not built to withstand water exposure and may malfunction as a result.
rn
rn6. Installation Conditions
rn- Installation and handling of the device should not be performed during a lightning storm to avoid the risk of electrical shock or damage.

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Preventive Measures

rnrn

1. Interference and Placement
rn- All wireless data transmission devices, including the G-100, may cause interference that can affect other nearby electronic devices.
rn- Ensure that the device is placed in a location that minimizes potential interference with other equipment.
rn
rn2. Qualified Personnel
rn- Only qualified and trained personnel should handle the connection and installation of the device. This is to ensure both personal safety and the integrity of the device.
rn
rn3. Firm Installation
rn- The device must be securely fastened in its predetermined location to prevent any movement that could disrupt its operation or cause damage.
rn
rn4. Programming & Power Supply
rn- Perform any programming tasks using a PC that has an independent power supply. This prevents any risk associated with power fluctuations or failures during the programming process.
rn
rn5. Water & Humidity
rn-The G-100 device is sensitive to water and humidity. Take measures to protect it from these elements to avoid internal damage.
rn
rn6. Maintain Device Cleanliness
rn- Keep the device clean and free from dust and debris to maintain optimal performance.
rn
rn7. Regular Inspection
rn- Regularly inspect the device and its connections to ensure they remain secure and in good condition.

title: SMS/GPRS Command Overview
discription:
The G-100 device is a versatile communication tool designed to receive commands via GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) and SMS (Short Message Service). GPRS enables the device to maintain a continuous internet connection for real-time data transmission and command reception, making it ideal for remote monitoring and control applications. SMS provides a reliable alternative for sending commands when GPRS connectivity is unavailable or limited.

rnrn

All commands are case sensitive.  

rnrn

While SMS commands are sent using recharges, GPRS commands are sent via internet. Another difference lies in their syntax. But their working & flow of execution of task is same. Clients can make use of the FOTAWEB platform which is an additional feature provided by the company for easy and fast configuration of devices on which these GPRS commands can be sent.

title: Steps to install SIM Card
discription:
To ensure a smooth initial setup of your device, follow these steps to correctly insert the SIM card:
