    rn
  • Open Flap: Locate the G-400 side flap on your device. Gently pull it out using the knob attached to the flap.
    • rn
  • Insert SIM in SIM Slot: Place the SIM card into the designated slot as illustrated in the device manual. Ensure that the cut-off corner of the SIM card is aligned correctly and pointing forward towards the slot.
    • rn
  • ON/ OFF: On SIM card insertion, the device will turn ON automatically and will work on the internal battery.
    • rn
  • Close the Flap: Once the device is switched ON after inserting the SIM, carefully reinsert the flap until it is securely closed.
    • rn

The device is now ready to be connected and powered on.

title: Quick SMS Configuration
discription:
The default configuration ensures optimal track quality and efficient data usage. Follow these steps to quickly set up your device via SMS commands.

rnrn

A. Commands to Change Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To port the device to a SERVER
rn- Command: #SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;<password>
rn- Example: #SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000;<6906>
rn- Description: This command directs the G-400 device to connect to the server specified by the given IP address and port number. In the example, the device will be configured to communicate with the server at IP 196.168.175.12 and port 20000.

rnrn

2. To change the APN settings
rn- Command: #CONFIG::APN::username::password;<password>
rn- Purpose: Configures your GPRS account settings.
rn- Details:

rnrn

- APN (Access Point Name): Used to access the GPRS gateway provided by your network operator.
rn- Username: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).
rn- Password: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).
rn- Example: For the Idea network without internet, the command would be: #CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>

rnrn

3. PPI Configuration
rn- Command: WEBSTART<xxx/H/M/S>,<yyy/H/M/S><password>
rn- Purpose: Start live tracking with different intervals depending on IGNITION ON ,IGNITION OFF interval respectively . H - Hours, M-Minutes, S- Seconds
rn- Example: WEBSTART030S,002M<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Commands to Check Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Check the GPRS Status
rn- Command: GPRSSTATUS<6906>
rn- Purpose: Retrieves the complete status of the device.

rnrn

rn- Speed: Indicates the speed of the vehicle in KPH.
rn- Date: The date of the recorded data.
rn- Time: The time of the recorded data in IST.

rnrn

To view the exact location on Google Maps, enter the latitude and longitude coordinates separated by a comma (,) in the search bar at [www.maps.google.com](http://www.maps.google.com). This will show the precise location on the map.

rnrn

3.To Check the Status of the System
rnCommand: SYSSTATUS<6906>
rnResponse: This command provides important system statuses, including:
rn- Main power status
rn- Ignition status
rn- Immobilizer status
rn- A/C status
rn- Door status
rn- Reserved low sense input
rn- Odometer (KM)
rn- Onboard temperature
rn- Internal battery voltage

rnrn

 

rnrn

C. FE<6906>: 

rnrn

This Command is used to clear the unsent memory data from flash.

rnrn

 

rnrn

D. FR<6906>:

rnrn

This Command is used to set factory default values. After this, all the user configured settings will be erased and factory fitted values will be implemented.

rnrn

 

rnrn

E. Default Configuration Settings

rnrn

1. Movement and Ignition Detection

rnrn

- Movement Detection: The device detects vehicle movement using the accelerometer.
rn- Ignition Detection: The ignition is detected by the vehicle's power voltage, which should range between 8 and 55 volts.

rnrn

2. Device Recording on Movement
rn- Recording Conditions: When the vehicle covers a distance of at least 50 meters while in idle mode, the device will begin tracking the movement of the vehicle.
rn- Stop Detection: The device will mark the vehicle as stopped if it remains stationary for one continuous minute.

rnrn

3. Device Recording on Stop
rn- Recording Conditions: If the vehicle remains stationary for one continuous minute, the device will mark it as stopped.(Speed 0kmph and no signal from motion sensors/accelerometer)

rnrn

4. Sending Records to Server
rn- Data Transmission: Once a record is made, it is sent to the server according to the default settings. Data can be sent based on specific criteria such as set time intervals, alerts, angle changes, and distance traveled.

rnrn

5. Synchronization and Updates
rnAfter a successful SMS configuration, the G-400 device will synchronize its time and update the records to the configured server. Users can modify time intervals and default I/O elements using the Atlanta Configurator tool or additional SMS commands. This ensures that the device remains accurate and up-to-date, providing reliable data for monitoring vehicle movement and status.

title: Installation Guidelines
discription:
1. Connecting Wires

rnrn

- Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.
rn- Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.
rn- Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.
rn- Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source

rnrn

- Power Retention During Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.
rn- Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.
rn- Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and rotection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire

rnrn

- Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.
rn- Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.
rn- Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire

rnrn

- Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.
rn- Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.
rn- Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

*RELAY DIAGRAM*

rnrn

 

rnrn

Relay Wiring Diagram Explanation

rnrn

To properly connect the relay for your device, follow these detailed instructions:
rn1. Pin 85
rnConnect the wire on pin 85 pin with the power source. Ensure that the power supply voltage matches the voltage requirements of your vehicle.
rn
rn2. Pin 87A (Normally Closed) and Pin 30 (Common Connection)
rn- Pin 30: You need to cut the vehicle’s ignition wire and connect one end to Pin 87A and connect ignition sense wire of the device.
rn- Pin 87A: Connect it to the ACC (Accessory), Vehicles/ Key Switch wire of your vehicle.
rn
rn3. Pin 86
rnConnect this pin to the device's ignition control wire. This wire controls the relay’s switching based on the ignition status.
rn
rnBy following these connections, you ensure that the relay is correctly wired to manage the ignition and power supply for your device, allowing for proper operation and control.

rnrn

 

rnrn

NOTE: Power Supply Connection Guidelines

rnrn

Optimal Connection Point
rnWhen connecting the power supply for the G-400 device, it is crucial to select a point with very low impedance on the vehicle's onboard network. Such points are typically found at the battery terminals of the car. This ensures stable voltage supply and minimizes the risk of electrical interference.
rn
rnRecommended Connection Methods
rn1. Direct Battery Terminal Connection: It is highly recommended to connect the G-400's power wires (GND and POWER) directly to the battery terminals. This direct connection provides a reliable and stable power source for the device.
rn2. Fuse Box Connection: Alternatively, you can connect the wires to the main POWER cable inside the vehicle's fuse box. Ensure that the fuse box is connected to the vehicle's computer power supply. This method also provides a controlled power supply environment.
rn
rnGround Connection Considerations
rn- GND Wire Connection: The GND wire must be connected to a designated point specifically designed for connecting vehicle computer grounds. Avoid arbitrary grounding to the car's mass, as this can introduce unpredictable static and dynamic potentials, potentially leading to unstable operation or failure of the G-400 device.
rn
rnBy adhering to these detailed connection guidelines, you can ensure the proper and reliable operation of the G-400 device within your vehicle's electrical system. Always prioritize stable connections and avoid any practices that could compromise the device's performance or safety.

rn

title: Safety Instructions
discription:
Operating the G-400 device safely requires careful attention to the following guidelines and recommendations. Adhering to these instructions will help you avoid hazardous situations and ensure the optimal performance of your device. Please read and follow these instructions meticulously before operating the device.

rnrn

A. Safety instructions

rnrn

1. Power Specifications
rn- The G-400 device operates on a nominal voltage of +12 VDC/+24 VDC.
rn- The allowable voltage range for safe operation is between +8 V DC and +36 V DC.

rnrn


rn2. Transportation and Handling
rn- To prevent mechanical damage during transportation, ensure that the device is packaged in an impact-resistant container.
rn- When setting up the device, place it in a location where the LED indicators are clearly visible. These indicators provide essential information about the device's operational status.
rn
rn3. Connection and Disconnection Procedures
rn- When connecting the wiring cables to the vehicle, make sure to disconnect the relevant jumpers from the vehicle's power supply first.
rn- Before removing the device from the vehicle, always disconnect the wiring harness connection to prevent any electrical hazards.
rn
rn4. Mounting Instructions
rn- The device should be installed in a restricted access area, ensuring that it remains out of reach of the operator during normal operation.
rn- Secure the device firmly in its designated location to prevent any accidental displacement.
rn- The device should be installed with a sky view and kept away from metal surfaces.
rn
rn5. Water Exposure
rn- Avoid exposing the device directly to water, as it is not built to withstand water exposure and may malfunction as a result.
rn
rn6. Installation Conditions
rn- Installation and handling of the device should not be performed during a lightning storm to avoid the risk of electrical shock or damage.

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Preventive Measures

rnrn

1. Interference and Placement
rn- All wireless data transmission devices, including the G-400, may cause interference that can affect other nearby electronic devices.
rn- Ensure that the device is placed in a location that minimizes potential interference with other equipment.
rn
rn2. Qualified Personnel
rn- Only qualified and trained personnel should handle the connection and installation of the device. This is to ensure both personal safety and the integrity of the device.
rn
rn3. Firm Installation
rn- The device must be securely fastened in its predetermined location to prevent any movement that could disrupt its operation or cause damage.
rn
rn4. Programming & Power Supply
rn- Perform any programming tasks using a PC that has an independent power supply. This prevents any risk associated with power fluctuations or failures during the programming process.
rn
rn5. Water & Humidity
rn-The G-400 device is sensitive to water and humidity. Take measures to protect it from these elements to avoid internal damage.
rn
rn6. Maintain Device Cleanliness
rn- Keep the device clean and free from dust and debris to maintain optimal performance.
rn
rn7. Regular Inspection
rn- Regularly inspect the device and its connections to ensure they remain secure and in good condition.

title: Sleep Modes
discription:
The VTC-100 device supports four different sleep modes:

rnrn
    rn
  • GPS Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Online Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Ultra Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
rnrn

These modes are designed to reduce the device’s power consumption when the vehicle is not in operation.

rnrn

1. GPS Sleep Mode

rnrn

The VTC-100 can enter GPS Sleep Mode if this mode is enabled in the configuration settings.

rnrn

The sleep timeout starts counting once the device enters STOP mode. After the configured timeout is reached and all required conditions for GPS Sleep Mode are satisfied, the device transitions into sleep mode.

rnrn

Note: Screenshot from Configurator.

rnrn

When operating in GPS Sleep Mode, the VTC-100 turns off the GPS module while continuing to create new periodic records. This helps reduce power consumption and conserves the vehicle battery.

rnrn

The VTC-100 enters GPS Sleep Mode when all of the following conditions are met:

rnrn
    rn
  • The device is configured to operate in GPS Sleep Mode, and the sleep timeout has been reached.
    • rn
  • The device time must be synchronized with GPS satellites. Starting from firmware ATL-VTC-100-V0.2, this requirement depends on the “Records saving/sending without TS” parameter:rn
      rn
    • After Position Fix – The VTC-100 time is synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix is obtained.
      • rn
    • After Time Sync – The VTC-100 time is synchronized via NTP, NITZ, or GNSS satellites.
      • rn
    • Always – The VTC-100 will enter sleep mode even without time synchronization or GPS fix.
      • rn
    rn
    • rn
  • No movement is detected by the accelerometer or the configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is off.
    • rn
  • No SMS messages are being received.
    • rn
rnrn

Note: In firmware versions older than ATL-VTC-100-V0.2.0, the device time must be synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix must be obtained before the device can enter GPS Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-100 exits GPS Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

2. Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

When the VTC-100 enters Deep Sleep Mode, the GNSS receiver is set to sleep mode, and the GSM/GPRS module is turned off. As a result, it is not possible to wake the device via SMS.

rnrn

Even in this mode, the device continues to save records with the last known coordinates and sends them to the AVL server. To transmit data, the GSM/GPRS module is temporarily turned on and then switched off again after the data is sent. This approach helps reduce power consumption and conserve the vehicle’s battery.

rnrn

Note: Screenshot from Configurator.

rnrn

Power saving in Deep Sleep Mode depends on two configurable parameters:

rnrn
    rn
  • Send Period
    • rn
  • Minimum Record Saving Period under “X on Stop Mode”
    • rn
rnrn

When records are successfully sent while in Deep Sleep Mode, the Open Link Timeout counter is skipped, allowing the VTC-100 to immediately return to Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

Because many functions are disabled during Deep Sleep Mode, the following I/O elements are not included in records generated in this mode:

rnrn
    rn
  • GSM Signal
    • rn
  • GNSS Status
    • rn
  • GNSS PDOP
    • rn
  • GNSS HDOP
    • rn
  • GSM CellID
    • rn
  • GSM Area Code
    • rn
  • Active GSM Operator
    • rn
  • Trip Odometer
    • rn
  • Total Odometer
    • rn
  • Speed
    • rn
  • Fuel Rate GPS
    • rn
  • Fuel Used GPS
    • rn
  • ICCID
    • rn
rnrn

The VTC-100 can enter Deep Sleep Mode when all of the following conditions are satisfied:

rnrn
    rn
  • The device is configured for Deep Sleep Mode, and the sleep timeout has been reached.
    • rn
  • The device time must be synchronized with GPS satellites. Starting from firmware ATL-VTC-100-V0.2, this depends on the “Records saving/sending without TS” parameter:rn
      rn
    • After Position Fix – VTC-100 time is synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix is obtained.
      • rn
    • After Time Sync – VTC-100 time is synchronized through NTP, NITZ, or GNSS satellites.
      • rn
    • Always – VTC-100 can enter sleep mode without time synchronization or GPS fix.
      • rn
    rn
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is off.
    • rn
  • No movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Minimum Record Saving Period (Data Acquisition Mode settings) must be greater than the Open Link Timeout parameter, allowing the VTC-100 to close the GPRS link.
    • rn
  • The difference between Send Period (Data Acquisition Mode settings) and Open Link Timeout must be more than 90 seconds, allowing the device to close the GPRS link within at least 90 seconds.
    • rn
  • No SMS messages are being received.
    • rn
  • Data socket(s) are closed.
    • rn
  • Data sending is not in progress.
    • rn
  • FOTA is not in progress.
    • rn
rnrn

Note: In firmware versions older than ATL-VTC-100-V0.2, the device time must be synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix must be obtained before the device can enter Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-100 exits Deep Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

3. Online Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

In Online Deep Sleep Mode, the VTC-100 operates similarly to Deep Sleep Mode, but remains registered on the GSM network. The GSM module stays powered, resulting in higher power consumption compared to standard Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

In this mode, the device can:

rnrn
    rn
  • Send and receive SMS messages
    • rn
  • Make or receive calls
    • rn
rnrn

Additionally, if a GPRS context was previously opened, it remains active and is not closed.

rnrn

Note: Screenshot from Configurator.

rnrn

The conditions required to enter Online Deep Sleep Mode are the same as those for entering Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-100 exits Online Deep Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

4. Ultra Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

In Ultra Deep Sleep Mode, both the GPS module and GSM modem are turned off, and most device functions are suspended to achieve maximum battery saving.

rnrn

The conditions required to enter Ultra Deep Sleep Mode are the same as those for entering Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-100 exits Ultra Deep Sleep Mode only when:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer, or
    • rn
  • I/O inputs detect activity
    • rn
rnrn

In this mode, movement source configuration and ignition source configuration are not taken into account.

rnrn

Note: Screenshot from Configurator.

title: Quick SMS configuration guide
discription:
The default configuration ensures optimal track quality and efficient data usage. Follow these steps to quickly set up your device via SMS commands.

rnrn

A. Commands to Change Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Port the Device to a Server

rnrn

   - Command: #SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;

rnrn

   - Example: #SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000; <6906>

rnrn

   - Description: This command directs the VTC-100 device to connect to the server specified by the given IP address and port number. In the example, the device will be  configured to communicate with the server at IP 196.168.175.12 and port 20000.

rnrn

 

rnrn

2. To Change the APN Settings

rnrn

- Command: #CONFIG::APN::username::password;

rnrn

- Purpose: Configures the APN settings of network service provider.

rnrn

- Details:

rnrn

  - APN (Access Point Name): Used to access the GPRS gateway provided by your network operator.

rnrn

  - Username: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Password: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Example: For the Idea network with APN internet, the command would be: #CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

3. Tracking Interval Configuration

rnrn

- Command: WEBSTARTxxx,yyy,zzz,z1z1z1

rnrn

- Purpose: Command to set the tracking interval and you will get confirmation SMS and then start sending data to the web server, where xxx stands for active(IGN ON) interval, yyy stands for passive(IGN OFF) interval, zzz stands for Main Power Removal interval and z1z1z1 stands for panic interval.

rnrn

H - Hours, M-Minutes, S- Seconds

rnrn

- Example: WEBSTART030S,030S,030S,030S<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Commands to Check Device Configuration  

rnrn

1. To Check the GPRS Status

rnrn

- Command: GPRSSTATUS<6906>

rnrn

- Purpose: Retrieves the complete status of the device.

rnrn

Description of the reply is as follows:

rnrnrn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn
EntriesDescriptionRemark
CN:Current network 
WTON-Web tracking intervalWeb tracking interval
DTOFFDistance based trackingSet distance would be shown here with DBTON
SOFFSleep statusSOFF for SLEEPOFF and SON for SLEEPON
MUC1:Internal memory unsent data count for first serverMUC1:75, Means 75 unsent packets in memory for first server
MUC2:Internal memory unsent data count for second serverMUC2:25, Means 25 unsent packets in memory for second server
CC:Current APN configurationCurrently using APN, UN, PWD

rnrn

2. To Get GPS Details

rnrn

Send the command `GETGPS` to the VTC-100 device.

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are unreachable: You will receive the message "GPS NOT FOUND."

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are reachable: You will receive a web link to view the location on a map.

rnrn

Additionally, you will receive the following information:

rnrn

- IMEI: Indicates the IMEI number of device.

rnrn

- ICCID: The ICCID of the SIM card used in the device.

rnrn

- Speed: Indicates the speed of the vehicle in KPH.

rnrn

- Date: The date of the recorded data.

rnrn

- Time: The time of the recorded data in IST.

rnrn

   To view the exact location on Google Maps, Click the link in the response or enter the latitude and longitude coordinates separated by a comma (,) in the search bar at [www.maps.google.com](http://www.maps.google.com). This will show the precise location on the map.

rnrn

 

rnrn

3. To Check the Status of the System

rnrn

rnrn

rnrn

E. Default Configuration Settings

rnrn

1. Movement and Ignition Detection

rnrn

- Movement Detection: The device detects vehicle movement using the accelerometer/IGNITION.

rnrn

- Ignition Detection: The ignition is detected by the vehicle's power voltage, which should range between 8 and 90 volts.

rnrn

 

rnrn

2. Device Recording on Movement

rnrn

- Recording Conditions: When the vehicle covers a distance of at least 50 meters while in idle mode, the device will begin tracking the movement of the vehicle.

rnrn

- Stop Detection: The device will mark the vehicle as stopped if it remains stationary for one continuous minute.

rnrn

 

rnrn

3. Device Recording on Stop

rnrn

- Recording Conditions: If the vehicle remains stationary for one continuous minute, the device will mark it as stopped. (speed 0 kmph and no signal from motion sensors/accelerometer)

rnrn

 

rnrn

4. Sending Records to Server

rnrn

- Data Transmission: Once a record is made, it is sent to the server according to the default settings. Data can be sent based on specific criteria such as set time intervals, alerts, angle changes, and distance traveled.

rnrn

 

rnrn

5. Synchronization and Updates

rnrn

After a successful SMS configuration, the VTC-100 device will synchronize its time and update the records to the configured server. Users can modify time intervals and default I/O elements using the Atlanta Configurator tool or additional SMS commands. This ensures that the device remains accurate and up-to-date, providing reliable data for monitoring vehicle movement and status.

title: Mounting Recommendations
discription:
1. Connecting Wires:

rnrn

   - Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.

rnrn

   - Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.

rnrn

   - Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source:

rnrn

   - Power Retention during Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.

rnrn

   - Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.

rnrn

   - Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and protection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire:

rnrn

   - Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.

rnrn

   - Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.

rnrn

   - Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire:

rnrn

   - Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.

rnrn

   - Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

INSTALLATION GUIDE

rnrn

Install the device under the dashboard with a clear sky view. Avoid metal surfaces to prevent signal interference. Ensure the device is securely mounted and properly connected to power and data sources.

rnrn

title: Relay Connections
discription:
To properly connect the relay for your device, follow these detailed instructions:

rnrn

1. Pin 85

rnrn

Connect the wire on pin 85 to the power source. Ensure that the power supply voltage matches the voltage requirements of your vehicle.

rnrn

2. Pin 87A (Normally Closed) and Pin 30 (Common Connection)

rnrn

   - Pin 30: You need to cut the vehicle’s ignition wire and connect one end to Pin 87A, and connect the ignition sense wire of the device.

rnrn

   - Pin 87A: Connect it to the ACC (Accessory), Vehicles/ Key Switch wire of your vehicle.

rnrn

3. Pin 86

rnrn

Connect this pin to the device's ignition control wire. This wire controls the relay’s switching based on the ignition status.

rnrn

By following these connections, you ensure that the relay is correctly wired to manage the ignition and power supply for your device, allowing for proper operation and control.

rnrn

 

rnrn

NOTE: Power Supply Connection Guidelines

rnrn

1. Optimal Connection Point

rnrn

When connecting the power supply for the VTC-100 device, it is crucial to select a point with very low impedance on the vehicle's onboard network. Such points are typically found at the battery terminals of the car. This ensures a stable voltage supply and minimizes the risk of electrical interference.

rnrn

2. Recommended Connection Methods

rnrn
    rn
  1. Direct Battery Terminal Connection: It is highly recommended to connect the VTC-100’s power wires (GND and POWER) directly to the battery terminals. This direct connection provides a reliable and stable power source for the device.
    2. rn
  2. Fuse Box Connection: Alternatively, you can connect the wires to the main POWER cable inside the vehicle's fuse box. Ensure that the fuse box is connected to the vehicle's computer power supply. This method also provides a controlled power supply environment.
    3. rn
rnrn

3. Ground Connection Considerations

rnrn

- GND Wire Connection: The GND wire must be connected to a designated point specifically designed for connecting vehicle computer grounds. Avoid arbitrary grounding to the car's mass, as this can introduce unpredictable static and dynamic potentials, potentially leading to unstable operation or failure of the VTC-100 device.

rnrn

By adhering to these detailed connection guidelines, you can ensure the proper and reliable operation of the VTC-100 device within your vehicle's electrical system. Always prioritize stable connections and avoid any practices that could compromise the device's performance or safety.

rnrn

title: Quick SMS configuration guide
discription:
The default configuration ensures optimal track quality and efficient data usage. Follow these steps to quickly set up your device via SMS commands.

rnrn

A. Commands to Change Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Port the Device to a Server

rnrn

   - Command: #SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;

rnrn

   - Example: #SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000; <6906>

rnrn

   - Description: This command directs the VTC-110 device to connect to the server specified by the given IP address and port number. In the example, the device will be  configured to communicate with the server at IP 196.168.175.12 and port 20000.

rnrn

 

rnrn

2. To Change the APN Settings

rnrn

- Command: #CONFIG::APN::username::password;

rnrn

- Purpose: Configures the APN settings of network service provider.

rnrn

- Details:

rnrn

  - APN (Access Point Name): Used to access the GPRS gateway provided by your network operator.

rnrn

  - Username: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Password: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Example: For the Idea network with APN internet, the command would be: #CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

3. Tracking Interval Configuration

rnrn

- Command: WEBSTART<xxx/H/M/S>,<yyy/H/M/S>,<zzz/H/M/S><password>

rnrn

- Purpose: Command to set the tracking interval and you will get confirmation SMS and then start sending data to the web server, where xxx stands for active(IGN ON) interval, yyy stands for passive(IGN OFF) interval, zzz stands for Main Power Removal interval and z1z1z1 stands for panic interval.H - Hours, M-Minutes, S- Seconds

rnrn

2. To Get GPS Details

Send the command `GETGPS` to the VTC-110 device.

rnrn

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are reachable: You will receive a web link to view the location on a map.

rnrn

- ICCID: The ICCID of the SIM card used in the device.

- Date: The date of the recorded data.

rnrn

- Time: The time of the recorded data in IST.

   To view the exact location on Google Maps, Click the link in the response or enter the latitude and longitude coordinates separated by a comma (,) in the search bar at [www.maps.google.com](http://www.maps.google.com). This will show the precise location on the map.

This Command is used to set factory default values. After this, all the user configured settings will be erased and factory fitted values will be implemented.

rnrn

 

rnrn

E. Default Configuration Settings

rnrn

1. Movement and Ignition Detection

rnrn

- Movement Detection: The device detects vehicle movement using the accelerometer/IGNITION.

rnrn

- Ignition Detection: The ignition is detected by the vehicle's power voltage, which should range between 8 and 90 volts.

rnrn

 

rnrn

2. Device Recording on Movement

rnrn

- Recording Conditions: When the vehicle covers a distance of at least 50 meters while in idle mode, the device will begin tracking the movement of the vehicle.

rnrn

- Stop Detection: The device will mark the vehicle as stopped if it remains stationary for one continuous minute.

rnrn

 

rnrn

3. Device Recording on Stop

rnrn

- Recording Conditions: If the vehicle remains stationary for one continuous minute, the device will mark it as stopped. (speed 0 kmph and no signal from motion sensors/accelerometer)

rnrn

 

rnrn

4. Sending Records to Server

rnrn

- Data Transmission: Once a record is made, it is sent to the server according to the default settings. Data can be sent based on specific criteria such as set time intervals, alerts, angle changes, and distance traveled.

rnrn

 

rnrn

5. Synchronization and Updates

rnrn

After a successful SMS configuration, the VTC-110 device will synchronize its time and update the records to the configured server. Users can modify time intervals and default I/O elements using the Atlanta Configurator tool or additional SMS commands. This ensures that the device remains accurate and up-to-date, providing reliable data for monitoring vehicle movement and status.

title: Mounting Recommendations
discription:
1. Connecting Wires:

rnrn

   - Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.

rnrn

   - Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.

rnrn

   - Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source:

rnrn

   - Power Retention during Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.

rnrn

   - Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.

rnrn

   - Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and protection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire:

rnrn

   - Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.

rnrn

   - Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.

rnrn

   - Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire:

rnrn

   - Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.

rnrn

   - Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

INSTALLATION GUIDE

rnrn

Install the device under the dashboard with a clear sky view. Avoid metal surfaces to prevent signal interference. Ensure the device is securely mounted and properly connected to power and data sources.

rnrn

title: SMS/GPRS Command Overview
discription:
The VTC-110 device is a versatile communication tool designed to receive commands via GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) and SMS (Short Message Service). GPRS enables the device to maintain a continuous internet connection for real-time data transmission and command reception, making it ideal for remote monitoring and control applications. SMS provides a reliable alternative for sending commands when GPRS connectivity is unavailable or limited.

rnrn

All commands are case sensitive.  

rnrn

While SMS commands are sent using recharges, GPRS commands are sent via the internet. Another difference lies in their syntax. But their working & flow of execution of the task is the same. Clients can make use of the FOTAWEB platform, which is an additional feature provided by the company for easy and fast configuration of devices on which these GPRS commands can be sent.

title: Micro SIM Card Installation and Battery Placement
meta_description: Micro SIM Card Installation and Battery Placement
discription:
To ensure a smooth initial setup of your device, follow these steps to correctly insert the SIM card and place the battery:

rnrn

A) SIM CARD INSERTION

rnrn

rnOpen the flap as shown to insert the SIM card into the SIM holder.

rnUnscrew all the screws on the back panel to remove the cabinet cover.

rnrn

rnUnlock the lock as shown below to open the cabinet.

rnrn

rnPeel off the protective layer from the adhesive tape provided for battery mounting.

rnCarefully position the battery inside the VTC-090 casing and press it gently so that the adhesive tape secures the battery firmly in place.

rnAfter installing the SIM card and placing the battery, switch the device to the ON position to start its operation.

title: SMS/GPRS Command Overview
discription:
The VTC-090 device is a versatile communication tool designed to receive commands via GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) and SMS (Short Message Service). GPRS enables the device to maintain a continuous internet connection for real-time data transmission and command reception, making it ideal for remote monitoring and control applications. SMS provides a reliable alternative for sending commands when GPRS connectivity is unavailable or limited.

rnrn

All commands are case sensitive.  

rnrn

While SMS commands are sent using recharges, GPRS commands are sent via the internet. Another difference lies in their syntax. But their working & flow of execution of the task is the same. Clients can make use of the FOTAWEB platform, which is an additional feature provided by the company for easy and fast configuration of devices on which these GPRS commands can be sent.

rnrn

Server Settings#SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;<password>Point the device to a server with a specified IP and port.#SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000;<6906>
#SERVERCHANGE1::IP::PORT;<password>Point the device to the second server with the specified IP and port. To enable the dual IP data sending mode#SERVERCHANGE1::196.168.175.12::20000;<6906>
#SERVERCHANGE1::--;<password>To remove the second IP, disable the Dual IP data sending mode#SERVERCHANGE1::--;<6906>
GPRS / APN Settings#CONFIG::APN::username::password;<password>Configure the GPRS account with APN, username, and password provided by the network operator.#CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>
#CONFIG?<password>Check the APN configuration of the device. Responds with saved GPRS APN, username, and password.#CONFIG?<6906>
Odometer ConfigurationSETODO::xxxxx;<password>Set the odometer to the present vehicle reading.SETODO::12345;<6906>
SETODO?<password>Get the current odometer value.SETODO?<6906>
Harsh Event CommandsHT::HA::HB::angle;<password>This command is used to set threshold values for sensing harsh turns, harsh braking, and harsh accelerationHT::005::005::020;<6906>
HT?<password>Enquire current harsh event thresholds.HT?<6906>
HT--;<password>Remove harsh event thresholds.HT--;<6909>
Overspeed AlertSPEED?<password>Check overspeed threshold.SPEED?<6906>
SPEED--;<password>Remove overspeed threshold.SPEED--;<6906>
SPEED::XXX;<password>Set the overspeed limit in KMPH.SPEED::100;<6906>
GMT ShiftGMS::xxxxx;<password>Set the GMT offset in minutes.GMT::330;<6906>
Password ChangePW::NewPassword;<DefaultPassword>Change the default password to a custom one. The password should be a four-digit number.PW::1234;<6906>
Vehicle ImmobilizerARM<password>Activate ARM mode. Cuts Ignition/Turn ON relay.ARM<6906>
DISARM<password>Deactivate ARM mode. Connect Ignition/Turn OFF Relay.DISARM<6906>
PPI ConfigurationWEBSTART<xxx/H/M/S>,<yyy/H/M/S>,<zzz/H/M/S>,<z1z1z1/H/M/S><password>Command to set the tracking interval, and you will get a confirmation SMS, and then start sending data to our web server, where xxx stands for active(IGN ON) interval, yyy stands for passive(IGN OFF) interval, zzz stands for Main Power Removal interval, and z1z1z1 stands for panic interval.WEBSTART030S,030S,030S,030S<6906>
Distance-Based TrackingDBT<xxxM/K><password>Enable distance-based tracking. Sends data to the server after covering the set distance and on deviation from the normal course. M-Meters, K-KilometersDBT500M<6906>
SDBT<password>Stop distance and angle-based tracking.SDBT<6906>
Output ON/OFFGOUTON<password>The device will lock the motor, and the Motor will not work after this command.GOUTON<6909>
GOUTOFF<password>The device will unlock the motor, and the Motor starts working GOUTOFF<6909>
BLE Sensor SettingsBLEMAC::MAC::X;<password>To set the MAC address of sensors to capture the data. Here, MAC stands for the MAC address of the sensor, and X stands for sensor type.
rn X=1 for Escort
rn X=2  for Fantom
rn X=3 for Strela / Pector		BLEMAC::ADECB123CBA2::2;<6906>
Movement Detection SettingsLOCKLATLONG::X;<password>Command to set the source of movement and enter idle mode
rn X=0  No lock(Always in motion)
rn X=1 Lock on IGNITION
rn X=2 Lock on Accelerometer		LOCKLATLONG::2;<6906>
Check Device Status
GPRS StatusGPRSSTATUS<password>Check the complete GPRS status.GPRSSTATUS<6906>
GPS DetailsGETGPS<password>Get GPS details. Responds with a GPS location link if satellites are reachable.GETGPS<6906>
System StatusSYSSTATUS<password>Check the system status, including power, ignition, immobilizer, PANIC, door status, odometer, temperature, and battery voltage.SYSSTATUS<6906>
Firmware VersionVERSION<password>Check firmware & hardware version.VERSION<6906>
Memory & Factory Settings
Clear MemoryFE<password>Clear unsent data from memory.FE<6906>
Factory ResetFR<password>Reset device to factory defaults.FR<6906>

title: Sleep Modes
discription:
The VTC-090 device supports four different sleep modes:

rnrn
    rn
  • GPS Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Online Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Ultra Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
rnrn

These modes are designed to reduce the device’s power consumption when the vehicle is not in operation.

rnrn

1. GPS Sleep Mode

rnrn

The VTC-090 can enter GPS Sleep Mode if this mode is enabled in the configuration settings.

rnrn

The sleep timeout starts counting once the device enters STOP mode. After the configured timeout is reached and all required conditions for GPS Sleep Mode are satisfied, the device transitions into sleep mode.

rnrn

When operating in GPS Sleep Mode, the VTC-090 turns off the GPS module while continuing to create new periodic records. This helps reduce power consumption and conserves the vehicle battery.

rnrn

The VTC-090 enters GPS Sleep Mode when all of the following conditions are met:

rnrn
    rn
  • The device is configured to operate in GPS Sleep Mode, and the sleep timeout has been reached.
    • rn
  • The device time must be synchronized with GPS satellites. Starting from firmware ATL-VTC-090-V0.2, this requirement depends on the “Records saving/sending without TS” parameter:rn
      rn
    • After Position Fix – The VTC-090 time is synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix is obtained.
      • rn
    • After Time Sync – The VTC-090 time is synchronized via NTP, NITZ, or GNSS satellites.
      • rn
    • Always – The VTC-090 will enter sleep mode even without time synchronization or GPS fix.
      • rn
    rn
    • rn
  • No movement is detected by the accelerometer or the configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is off.
    • rn
  • No SMS messages are being received.
    • rn
rnrn

Note: In firmware versions older than ATL-VTC-090-V0.2.0, the device time must be synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix must be obtained before the device can enter GPS Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-090 exits GPS Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

2. Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

When the VTC-090 enters Deep Sleep Mode, the GNSS receiver is set to sleep mode, and the GSM/GPRS module is turned off. As a result, it is not possible to wake the device via SMS.

rnrn

Even in this mode, the device continues to save records with the last known coordinates and sends them to the AVL server. To transmit data, the GSM/GPRS module is temporarily turned on and then switched off again after the data is sent. This approach helps reduce power consumption and conserve the vehicle’s battery.

rnrn

Power saving in Deep Sleep Mode depends on two configurable parameters:

rnrn
    rn
  • Send Period
    • rn
  • Minimum Record Saving Period under “X on Stop Mode”
    • rn
rnrn

When records are successfully sent while in Deep Sleep Mode, the Open Link Timeout counter is skipped, allowing the VTC-090 to immediately return to Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

Because many functions are disabled during Deep Sleep Mode, the following I/O elements are not included in records generated in this mode:

rnrn
    rn
  • GSM Signal
    • rn
  • GNSS Status
    • rn
  • GNSS PDOP
    • rn
  • GNSS HDOP
    • rn
  • GSM CellID
    • rn
  • GSM Area Code
    • rn
  • Active GSM Operator
    • rn
  • Trip Odometer
    • rn
  • Total Odometer
    • rn
  • Speed
    • rn
  • Fuel Rate GPS
    • rn
  • Fuel Used GPS
    • rn
  • ICCID
    • rn
rnrn

The VTC-090 can enter Deep Sleep Mode when all of the following conditions are satisfied:

rnrn
    rn
  • The device is configured for Deep Sleep Mode, and the sleep timeout has been reached.
    • rn
  • The device time must be synchronized with GPS satellites. Starting from firmware ATL-VTC-090-V0.2, this depends on the “Records saving/sending without TS” parameter:rn
      rn
    • After Position Fix – VTC-090 time is synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix is obtained.
      • rn
    • After Time Sync – VTC-090 time is synchronized through NTP, NITZ, or GNSS satellites.
      • rn
    • Always – VTC-090 can enter sleep mode without time synchronization or GPS fix.
      • rn
    rn
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is off.
    • rn
  • No movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Minimum Record Saving Period (Data Acquisition Mode settings) must be greater than the Open Link Timeout parameter, allowing the VTC-090 to close the GPRS link.
    • rn
  • The difference between Send Period (Data Acquisition Mode settings) and Open Link Timeout must be more than 90 seconds, allowing the device to close the GPRS link within at least 90 seconds.
    • rn
  • No SMS messages are being received.
    • rn
  • Data socket(s) are closed.
    • rn
  • Data sending is not in progress.
    • rn
  • FOTA is not in progress.
    • rn
rnrn

Note: In firmware versions older than ATL-VTC-090-V0.2, the device time must be synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix must be obtained before the device can enter Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-090 exits Deep Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

3. Online Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

In Online Deep Sleep Mode, the VTC-090 operates similarly to Deep Sleep Mode, but remains registered on the GSM network. The GSM module stays powered, resulting in higher power consumption compared to standard Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

In this mode, the device can:

rnrn
    rn
  • Send and receive SMS messages
    • rn
  • Make or receive calls
    • rn
rnrn

Additionally, if a GPRS context was previously opened, it remains active and is not closed.

rnrn

The conditions required to enter Online Deep Sleep Mode are the same as those for entering Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-090 exits Online Deep Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

4. Ultra Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

In Ultra Deep Sleep Mode, both the GPS module and GSM modem are turned off, and most device functions are suspended to achieve maximum battery saving.

rnrn

The conditions required to enter Ultra Deep Sleep Mode are the same as those for entering Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-090 exits Ultra Deep Sleep Mode only when:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer, or
    • rn
  • I/O inputs detect activity
    • rn
rnrn

In this mode, movement source configuration and ignition source configuration are not taken into account.

title: Mounting Recommendations
discription:
1. Connecting Wires:

rnrn

   - Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.

rnrn

   - Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.

rnrn

   - Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source:

rnrn

   - Power Retention during Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.

rnrn

   - Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.

rnrn

   - Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and protection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire:

rnrn

   - Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.

rnrn

   - Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.

rnrn

   - Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire:

rnrn

   - Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.

rnrn

   - Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

INSTALLATION GUIDE

rnrn

Install the device under the dashboard with a clear sky view. Avoid metal surfaces to prevent signal interference. Ensure the device is securely mounted and properly connected to power and data sources.

rnrn

title: Relay Connections
discription:
To properly connect the relay for your device, follow these detailed instructions:

rnrn

1. Pin 85

rnrn

Connect the wire on pin 85 to the power source. Ensure that the power supply voltage matches the voltage requirements of your vehicle.

rnrn

2. Pin 87A (Normally Closed) and Pin 30 (Common Connection)

rnrn

   - Pin 30: You need to cut the vehicle’s ignition wire and connect one end to Pin 87A, and connect the ignition sense wire of the device.

rnrn

   - Pin 87A: Connect it to the ACC (Accessory), Vehicles/ Key Switch wire of your vehicle.

rnrn

3. Pin 86

rnrn

Connect this pin to the device's ignition control wire. This wire controls the relay’s switching based on the ignition status.

rnrn

By following these connections, you ensure that the relay is correctly wired to manage the ignition and power supply for your device, allowing for proper operation and control.

rnrn

NOTE: Power Supply Connection Guidelines

rnrn

1. Optimal Connection Point

rnrn

When connecting the power supply for the VTC-090 device, it is crucial to select a point with very low impedance on the vehicle's onboard network. Such points are typically found at the battery terminals of the car. This ensures a stable voltage supply and minimizes the risk of electrical interference.

rnrn

2. Recommended Connection Methods

rnrn
    rn
  1. Direct Battery Terminal Connection: It is highly recommended to connect the VTC-090’s power wires (GND and POWER) directly to the battery terminals. This direct connection provides a reliable and stable power source for the device.
    2. rn
  2. Fuse Box Connection: Alternatively, you can connect the wires to the main POWER cable inside the vehicle's fuse box. Ensure that the fuse box is connected to the vehicle's computer power supply. This method also provides a controlled power supply environment.
    3. rn
rnrn

3. Ground Connection Considerations

rnrn

- GND Wire Connection: The GND wire must be connected to a designated point specifically designed for connecting vehicle computer grounds. Avoid arbitrary grounding to the car's mass, as this can introduce unpredictable static and dynamic potentials, potentially leading to unstable operation or failure of the VTC-090 device.

rnrn

By adhering to these detailed connection guidelines, you can ensure the proper and reliable operation of the VTC-090 device within your vehicle's electrical system. Always prioritize stable connections and avoid any practices that could compromise the device's performance or safety.

rnrn

title: Quick SMS configuration guide
discription:
The default configuration ensures optimal track quality and efficient data usage. Follow these steps to quickly set up your device via SMS commands.

rnrn

A. Commands to Change Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Port the Device to a Server

rnrn

   - Command: #SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;

rnrn

   - Example: #SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000; <6906>

rnrn

   - Description: This command directs the VTC-090 device to connect to the server specified by the given IP address and port number. In the example, the device will be  configured to communicate with the server at IP 196.168.175.12 and port 20000.

rnrn

 

rnrn

2. To Change the APN Settings

rnrn

- Command: #CONFIG::APN::username::password;

rnrn

- Purpose: Configures the APN settings of network service provider.

rnrn

- Details:

rnrn

  - APN (Access Point Name): Used to access the GPRS gateway provided by your network operator.

rnrn

  - Username: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Password: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Example: For the Idea network with APN internet, the command would be: #CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

3. Tracking Interval Configuration

rnrn

- Command: WEBSTARTxxx,yyy,zzz,z1z1z1

rnrn

- Purpose: Command to set the tracking interval and you will get confirmation SMS and then start sending data to the web server, where xxx stands for active(IGN ON) interval, yyy stands for passive (IGN OFF) interval, zzz stands for Main Power Removal interval and z1z1z1 stands for panic interval.

rnrn

H - Hours, M-Minutes, S- Seconds

rnrn

- Example: WEBSTART030S,030S,030S,030S<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

rnrn

1. To Check the GPRS Status

rnrn

- Command: GPRSSTATUS<6906>

rnrn

2. To Get GPS Details

rnrn

Send the command `GETGPS` to the VTC-090 device.

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are unreachable: You will receive the message "GPS NOT FOUND."

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are reachable: You will receive a web link to view the location on a map.

rnrn

Additionally, you will receive the following information:

rnrn

- IMEI: Indicates the IMEI number of device.

rnrn

rnrn

- Date: The date of the recorded data.

rnrn

rnrn

This Command is used to set factory default values. After this, all the user configured settings will be erased and factory fitted values will be implemented.

rnrn

 

rnrn

E. Default Configuration Settings

rnrn

1. Movement and Ignition Detection

rnrn

- Movement Detection: The device detects vehicle movement using the accelerometer/IGNITION.

rnrn

- Ignition Detection: The ignition is detected by the vehicle's power voltage, which should range between 8 and 90 volts.

rnrn

2. Device Recording on Movement

rnrn

- Recording Conditions: When the vehicle covers a distance of at least 50 meters while in idle mode, the device will begin tracking the movement of the vehicle.

rnrn

- Stop Detection: The device will mark the vehicle as stopped if it remains stationary for one continuous minute.

rnrn

3. Device Recording on Stop

rnrn

- Recording Conditions: If the vehicle remains stationary for one continuous minute, the device will mark it as stopped. (speed 0 kmph and no signal from motion sensors/accelerometer)

rnrn

4. Sending Records to Server

rnrn

- Data Transmission: Once a record is made, it is sent to the server according to the default settings. Data can be sent based on specific criteria such as set time intervals, alerts, angle changes, and distance traveled.

rnrn

5. Synchronization and Updates

rnrn

After a successful SMS configuration, the VTC-090 device will synchronize its time and update the records to the configured server. Users can modify time intervals and default I/O elements using the Atlanta Configurator tool or additional SMS commands. This ensures that the device remains accurate and up-to-date, providing reliable data for monitoring vehicle movement and status.

title: Relay Connections
discription:
To properly connect the relay for your device, follow these detailed instructions:

rnrn

1. Pin 85

rnrn

Connect the wire on pin 85 pin with the power source. Ensure that the power supply voltage matches the voltage requirements of your vehicle.

rnrn

2. Pin 87A (Normally Closed) and Pin 30 (Common Connection)

rnrn

   - Pin 30: You need to cut the vehicle’s ignition wire and connect one end to Pin 87A and connect ignition sense wire of the device

rnrn

   - Pin 87A: Connect it to the ACC (Accessory), Vehicles/ Key Switch wire of your vehicle.

rnrn

3. Pin 86

rnrn

Connect this pin to the device's ignition control wire. This wire controls the relay’s switching based on the ignition status.

rnrn

By following these connections, you ensure that the relay is correctly wired to manage the ignition and power supply for your device, allowing for proper operation and control.

rnrn

 

rnrn

NOTE: Power Supply Connection Guidelines

rnrn

1. Optimal Connection Point

rnrn

When connecting the power supply for the VTC-110 device, it is crucial to select a point with very low impedance on the vehicle's onboard network. Such points are typically found at the battery terminals of the car. This ensures stable voltage supply and minimizes the risk of electrical interference.

rnrn

2. Recommended Connection Methods

rnrn
    rn
  1. Direct Battery Terminal Connection: It is highly recommended to connect the VTC-110’s power wires (GND and POWER) directly to the battery terminals. This direct connection provides a reliable and stable power source for the device.
    2. rn
  2. Fuse Box Connection: Alternatively, you can connect the wires to the main POWER cable inside the vehicle's fuse box. Ensure that the fuse box is connected to the vehicle's computer power supply. This method also provides a controlled power supply environment.
    3. rn
rnrn

3. Ground Connection Considerations

rnrn

- GND Wire Connection: The GND wire must be connected to a designated point specifically designed for connecting vehicle computer grounds. Avoid arbitrary grounding to the car's mass, as this can introduce unpredictable static and dynamic potentials, potentially leading to unstable operation or failure of the VTC-110 device.

rnrn

By adhering to these detailed connection guidelines, you can ensure the proper and reliable operation of the VTC-110 device within your vehicle's electrical system. Always prioritize stable connections and avoid any practices that could compromise the device's performance or safety.

rnrn

title: Quick SMS configuration guide
discription:
The default configuration ensures optimal track quality and efficient data usage. Follow these steps to quickly set up your device via SMS commands.

rnrn

 A. Commands to Change Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Port the Device to a Server

rnrn

   - Command: #SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT; <password>

rnrn

   - Example: #SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000; <6906>

rnrn

   - Description: This command directs the ATC-500 device to connect to the server specified by the given IP address and port number. In the example, the device will be configured to communicate with the server at IP 196.168.175.12 and port 20000.

rnrn

2. To Change the APN Settings

rnrn

- Command: #CONFIG::APN::username::password; <password>

rnrn

- Purpose: Configures your GPRS account settings.

rnrn

- Details:

rnrn

  - APN (Access Point Name): Used to access the GPRS gateway provided by your network operator.

rnrn

  - Username: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Password: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

- Example: For the Idea network without internet, the command would be: #CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>

rnrn

3. PPI Configuration
rn- Command: WEBSTART<xxx/H/M/S><password>
rn- Purpose: Start live tracking and sending data on server where xxx stand for the interval and where  H - Hours, M-Minutes, S- Seconds
rn- Example: WEBSTART030S<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

B) Commands to Check Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Check the GPRS Status

rnrn

- Command: GPRSSTATUS<6906>

rnrn

- Purpose: Retrieves the complete status of the device.

rnrn

title: Safety information and precautions for operations
meta_description: Safety information and precautions for operations
discription:
Operating the ATC-500 device safely requires careful attention to the following guidelines and recommendations. Adhering to these instructions will help you avoid hazardous situations and ensure the optimal performance of your device. Please read and follow these instructions meticulously before operating the device.

rnrn

 

rnrn

A) Safety instructions

rnrn

1. Power Specifications

rnrn
    rn
  • The ATC-500 device charged up on using 5V Adapter.
    • rn
rnrn

2. Transportation and Handling

rnrn
    rn
  • To prevent mechanical damage during transportation, ensure that the device is packaged in an impact-resistant container.
    • rn
  • When setting up the device, place it in a location where the LED indicators are clearly visible. These indicators provide essential information about the device's operational status.
    • rn
rnrn

3. Water Exposure

rnrn
    rn
  • Avoid exposing the device directly to water, as it is not built to withstand water exposure and may malfunction as a result.
    • rn
rnrn

 

rnrn

B) PREVENTIVE MEASURES

rnrn

1. Interference and Placement

rnrn
    rn
  • All wireless data transmission devices, including the ATC-500, may cause interference that can affect other nearby electronic devices.
    • rn
  • Ensure that the device is placed in a location that minimizes potential interference with other equipment.
    • rn
rnrn

2. Qualified Personnel

rnrn
    rn
  • Only qualified and trained personnel should handle the connection and installation of the device. This is to ensure both personal safety and the integrity of the device.
    • rn
rnrn

 3. Firm Installation

rnrn
    rn
  • The device must be securely fastened in its predetermined location to prevent any movement that could disrupt its operation or cause damage.
    • rn
rnrn

4. Water & Humidity

rnrn
    rn
  • The ATC-500 device is sensitive to water and humidity. Take measures to protect it from these elements to avoid internal damage.
    • rn
rnrn

5. Maintain Device Cleanliness

rnrn
    rn
  • Keep the device clean and free from dust and debris to maintain optimal performance.
    • rn
rnrn

6. Regular Inspection

rnrn
    rn
  • Regularly inspect the device and its connections to ensure they remain secure and in good condition.
    • rn
rnrn

7. Battery

rnrn
    rn
  • Don’t remove or replace  the batteries
    • rn

title: Mounting recommendations
discription:
1. Connecting Wires:

rnrn

   - Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.

rnrn

   - Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.

rnrn

   - Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source:

rnrn

   - Power Retention during Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.

rnrn

   - Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.

rnrn

   - Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and protection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire:

rnrn

   - Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.

rnrn

   - Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.

rnrn

   - Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire:

rnrn

   - Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.

rnrn

   - Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

INSTALLATION GUIDE

rnrn

Install the device under the dashboard with a clear sky view. Avoid metal surfaces to prevent signal interference. Ensure the device is securely mounted and properly connected to power and data sources.

title: Overview

The VTC-110 is a power-packed 4G LTE Cat-1 vehicle tracking device designed specifically for electric vehicle (EV) fleets. With advanced 4G connectivity, 2G fallback, and Bluetooth support, it ensures reliable, uninterrupted data transmission across diverse operating conditions. Featuring a wide high-voltage operating range and CAN bus support, the VTC-110 delivers deep insights into battery performance, energy usage, and vehicle health. Built for high-performance EV tracking, it empowers fleet operators with real-time visibility, smarter battery management, and greater control over their electric mobility operations.

discription:
The VTC-300 device is equipped with a series of LED indicators that provide vital information about its operational status. Understanding these indicators is essential for effective monitoring and troubleshooting. Below is a detailed explanation of the LED statuses related to charging, network registration, and GPS fix:

rnrn

GSMGreenIndicates the network registration statusOFF: The device is offThe device is powered off.
