title: Sleep Modes
discription:
The VTC-300 device supports four different sleep modes:

rnrn
    rn
  • GPS Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Online Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Ultra Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
rnrn

These modes are designed to reduce the device’s power consumption when the vehicle is not in operation.

rnrn

1. GPS Sleep Mode

rnrn

The VTC-300 can enter GPS Sleep Mode if this mode is enabled in the configuration settings.

rnrn

The sleep timeout starts counting once the device enters STOP mode. After the configured timeout is reached and all required conditions for GPS Sleep Mode are satisfied, the device transitions into sleep mode.

rnrn

When operating in GPS Sleep Mode, the VTC-300 turns off the GPS module while continuing to create new periodic records. This helps reduce power consumption and conserves the vehicle battery.

rnrn

The VTC-300 enters GPS Sleep Mode when all of the following conditions are met:

rnrn
    rn
  • The device is configured to operate in GPS Sleep Mode, and the sleep timeout has been reached.
    • rn
  • The device time must be synchronized with GPS satellites. Starting from firmware ATL-VTC-300-V0.2, this requirement depends on the “Records saving/sending without TS” parameter:rn
      rn
    • After Position Fix – The VTC-300 time is synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix is obtained.
      • rn
    • After Time Sync – The VTC-300 time is synchronized via NTP, NITZ, or GNSS satellites.
      • rn
    • Always – The VTC-300 will enter sleep mode even without time synchronization or GPS fix.
      • rn
    rn
    • rn
  • No movement is detected by the accelerometer or the configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is off.
    • rn
  • No SMS messages are being received.
    • rn
rnrn

Note: In firmware versions older than ATL-VTC-300-V0.2.0, the device time must be synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix must be obtained before the device can enter GPS Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-300 exits GPS Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

2. Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

When the VTC-300 enters Deep Sleep Mode, the GNSS receiver is set to sleep mode, and the GSM/GPRS module is turned off. As a result, it is not possible to wake the device via SMS.

rnrn

Even in this mode, the device continues to save records with the last known coordinates and sends them to the AVL server. To transmit data, the GSM/GPRS module is temporarily turned on and then switched off again after the data is sent. This approach helps reduce power consumption and conserve the vehicle’s battery.

rnrn

Power saving in Deep Sleep Mode depends on two configurable parameters:

rnrn
    rn
  • Send Period
    • rn
  • Minimum Record Saving Period under “X on Stop Mode”
    • rn
rnrn

When records are successfully sent while in Deep Sleep Mode, the Open Link Timeout counter is skipped, allowing the VTC-300 to immediately return to Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

Because many functions are disabled during Deep Sleep Mode, the following I/O elements are not included in records generated in this mode:

rnrn
    rn
  • GSM Signal
    • rn
  • GNSS Status
    • rn
  • GNSS PDOP
    • rn
  • GNSS HDOP
    • rn
  • GSM CellID
    • rn
  • GSM Area Code
    • rn
  • Active GSM Operator
    • rn
  • Trip Odometer
    • rn
  • Total Odometer
    • rn
  • Speed
    • rn
  • Fuel Rate GPS
    • rn
  • Fuel Used GPS
    • rn
  • ICCID
    • rn
rnrn

The VTC-300 can enter Deep Sleep Mode when all of the following conditions are satisfied:

rnrn
    rn
  • The device is configured for Deep Sleep Mode, and the sleep timeout has been reached.
    • rn
  • The device time must be synchronized with GPS satellites. Starting from firmware ATL-VTC-300-V0.2, this depends on the “Records saving/sending without TS” parameter:rn
      rn
    • After Position Fix – VTC-300 time is synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix is obtained.
      • rn
    • After Time Sync – VTC-300 time is synchronized through NTP, NITZ, or GNSS satellites.
      • rn
    • Always – VTC-300 can enter sleep mode without time synchronization or GPS fix.
      • rn
    rn
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is off.
    • rn
  • No movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Minimum Record Saving Period (Data Acquisition Mode settings) must be greater than the Open Link Timeout parameter, allowing the VTC-300 to close the GPRS link.
    • rn
  • The difference between Send Period (Data Acquisition Mode settings) and Open Link Timeout must be more than 90 seconds, allowing the device to close the GPRS link within at least 90 seconds.
    • rn
  • No SMS messages are being received.
    • rn
  • Data socket(s) are closed.
    • rn
  • Data sending is not in progress.
    • rn
  • FOTA is not in progress.
    • rn
rnrn

Note: In firmware versions older than ATL-VTC-300-V0.2, the device time must be synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix must be obtained before the device can enter Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-300 exits Deep Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

3. Online Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

In Online Deep Sleep Mode, the VTC-300 operates similarly to Deep Sleep Mode, but remains registered on the GSM network. The GSM module stays powered, resulting in higher power consumption compared to standard Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

In this mode, the device can:

rnrn
    rn
  • Send and receive SMS messages
    • rn
  • Make or receive calls
    • rn
rnrn

Additionally, if a GPRS context was previously opened, it remains active and is not closed.

rnrn

The conditions required to enter Online Deep Sleep Mode are the same as those for entering Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-300 exits Online Deep Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

4. Ultra Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

In Ultra Deep Sleep Mode, both the GPS module and GSM modem are turned off, and most device functions are suspended to achieve maximum battery saving.

rnrn

The conditions required to enter Ultra Deep Sleep Mode are the same as those for entering Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-300 exits Ultra Deep Sleep Mode only when:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer, or
    • rn
  • I/O inputs detect activity
    • rn
rnrn

In this mode, movement source configuration and ignition source configuration are not taken into account.

title: SMS/GPRS Command Overview
discription:
The VTC-300 device is a versatile communication tool designed to receive commands via GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) and SMS (Short Message Service). GPRS enables the device to maintain a continuous internet connection for real-time data transmission and command reception, making it ideal for remote monitoring and control applications. SMS provides a reliable alternative for sending commands when GPRS connectivity is unavailable or limited.

rnrn

All commands are case sensitive.  

rnrn

While SMS commands are sent using recharges, GPRS commands are sent via the internet. Another difference lies in their syntax. But their working & flow of execution of the task is the same. Clients can make use of the FOTAWEB platform, which is an additional feature provided by the company for easy and fast configuration of devices on which these GPRS commands can be sent.

title: Device Configuration (Windows)
discription:
By default, the VTC-110 device is delivered with factory settings. These settings should be configured according to the specific requirements of the user or application.

rnrn

Device configuration is performed using the Atlanta Configurator software.

rnrn

System Requirements

rnrn

The Atlanta Configurator operates on Microsoft Windows operating systems and requires Microsoft .NET Framework 5.0 (32-bit or 64-bit) to be installed on the computer.

rnrn

Supported operating systems include:

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    Windows Vista

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Windows 7

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Windows 8.1

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Windows 10

    rn
    • rn
rnrn

Ensure that the required .NET Framework version is installed before launching the configurator.

rnrn

rnrn
    rn

    Download the latest VTC110 Configurator from the provided link.

    rn
    2. rn
  2. rn

  3. rn

  2. rn

title: Sleep Modes
discription:
The VTC-110 device supports four different sleep modes:

rnrn
    rn
  • GPS Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Online Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Ultra Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
rnrn

These modes are designed to reduce the device’s power consumption when the vehicle is not in operation.

rnrn

1. GPS Sleep Mode

rnrn

The VTC-110 can enter GPS Sleep Mode if this mode is enabled in the configuration settings.

rnrn

The sleep timeout starts counting once the device enters STOP mode. After the configured timeout is reached and all required conditions for GPS Sleep Mode are satisfied, the device transitions into sleep mode.

rnrn

Note: Screenshot from Configurator.

rnrn

When operating in GPS Sleep Mode, the VTC-110 turns off the GPS module while continuing to create new periodic records. This helps reduce power consumption and conserves the vehicle battery.

rnrn

The VTC-110 enters GPS Sleep Mode when all of the following conditions are met:

rnrn
    rn
  • The device is configured to operate in GPS Sleep Mode, and the sleep timeout has been reached.
    • rn
  • The device time must be synchronized with GPS satellites. Starting from firmware ATL-VTC-110-V0.2, this requirement depends on the “Records saving/sending without TS” parameter:rn
      rn
    • After Position Fix – The VTC-110 time is synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix is obtained.
      • rn
    • After Time Sync – The VTC-110 time is synchronized via NTP, NITZ, or GNSS satellites.
      • rn
    • Always – The VTC-110 will enter sleep mode even without time synchronization or GPS fix.
      • rn
    rn
    • rn
  • No movement is detected by the accelerometer or the configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is off.
    • rn
  • No SMS messages are being received.
    • rn
rnrn

Note: In firmware versions older than ATL-VTC-110-V0.2.0, the device time must be synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix must be obtained before the device can enter GPS Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-110 exits GPS Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

2. Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

When the VTC-110 enters Deep Sleep Mode, the GNSS receiver is set to sleep mode, and the GSM/GPRS module is turned off. As a result, it is not possible to wake the device via SMS.

rnrn

Even in this mode, the device continues to save records with the last known coordinates and sends them to the AVL server. To transmit data, the GSM/GPRS module is temporarily turned on and then switched off again after the data is sent. This approach helps reduce power consumption and conserve the vehicle’s battery.

rnrn

Note: Screenshot from Configurator.

rnrn

Power saving in Deep Sleep Mode depends on two configurable parameters:

rnrn
    rn
  • Send Period
    • rn
  • Minimum Record Saving Period under “X on Stop Mode”
    • rn
rnrn

When records are successfully sent while in Deep Sleep Mode, the Open Link Timeout counter is skipped, allowing the VTC-110 to immediately return to Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

Because many functions are disabled during Deep Sleep Mode, the following I/O elements are not included in records generated in this mode:

rnrn
    rn
  • GSM Signal
    • rn
  • GNSS Status
    • rn
  • GNSS PDOP
    • rn
  • GNSS HDOP
    • rn
  • GSM CellID
    • rn
  • GSM Area Code
    • rn
  • Active GSM Operator
    • rn
  • Trip Odometer
    • rn
  • Total Odometer
    • rn
  • Speed
    • rn
  • Fuel Rate GPS
    • rn
  • Fuel Used GPS
    • rn
  • ICCID
    • rn
rnrn

The VTC-110 can enter Deep Sleep Mode when all of the following conditions are satisfied:

rnrn
    rn
  • The device is configured for Deep Sleep Mode, and the sleep timeout has been reached.
    • rn
  • The device time must be synchronized with GPS satellites. Starting from firmware ATL-VTC-110-V0.2, this depends on the “Records saving/sending without TS” parameter:rn
      rn
    • After Position Fix – VTC-110 time is synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix is obtained.
      • rn
    • After Time Sync – VTC-110 time is synchronized through NTP, NITZ, or GNSS satellites.
      • rn
    • Always – VTC-110 can enter sleep mode without time synchronization or GPS fix.
      • rn
    rn
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is off.
    • rn
  • No movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Minimum Record Saving Period (Data Acquisition Mode settings) must be greater than the Open Link Timeout parameter, allowing the VTC-110 to close the GPRS link.
    • rn
  • The difference between Send Period (Data Acquisition Mode settings) and Open Link Timeout must be more than 90 seconds, allowing the device to close the GPRS link within at least 90 seconds.
    • rn
  • No SMS messages are being received.
    • rn
  • Data socket(s) are closed.
    • rn
  • Data sending is not in progress.
    • rn
  • FOTA is not in progress.
    • rn
rnrn

Note: In firmware versions older than ATL-VTC-110-V0.2, the device time must be synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix must be obtained before the device can enter Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-110 exits Deep Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

3. Online Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

In Online Deep Sleep Mode, the VTC-110 operates similarly to Deep Sleep Mode, but remains registered on the GSM network. The GSM module stays powered, resulting in higher power consumption compared to standard Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

In this mode, the device can:

rnrn
    rn
  • Send and receive SMS messages
    • rn
  • Make or receive calls
    • rn
rnrn

Additionally, if a GPRS context was previously opened, it remains active and is not closed.

rnrn

Note: Screenshot from Configurator.

rnrn

The conditions required to enter Online Deep Sleep Mode are the same as those for entering Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-110 exits Online Deep Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

4. Ultra Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

In Ultra Deep Sleep Mode, both the GPS module and GSM modem are turned off, and most device functions are suspended to achieve maximum battery saving.

rnrn

The conditions required to enter Ultra Deep Sleep Mode are the same as those for entering Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-110 exits Ultra Deep Sleep Mode only when:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer, or
    • rn
  • I/O inputs detect activity
    • rn
rnrn

In this mode, movement source configuration and ignition source configuration are not taken into account.

rnrn

Note: Screenshot from Configurator.

title: Micro SIM Card Installation and Battery Placement
meta_description: Micro SIM Card Installation and Battery Placement
discription:
To ensure a smooth initial setup of your device, follow these steps to correctly insert the SIM card and place the battery:

rnrn

1. Removing the Back Cover
rnUnscrew all the screws on the back panel to remove the cabinet cover.

rnrn

2. Unlock the cabinet
rnUnlock the lock as shown below to open the cabinet.

rnrn

3. Insert the SIM Card (if using Physical SIM):
rnPlace the Micro SIM card into the designated SIM slot as shown in the device manual. Ensure the cut corner of the SIM card is properly aligned with the slot.

rnrn

4. Remove Adhesive Protection
rnPeel off the protective layer from the adhesive tape provided for battery mounting.

rnrn

5. Place the Battery
rnCarefully position the battery inside the VTC-100 casing and press it gently so that the adhesive tape secures the battery firmly in place.

rnrn

6. Power On the Device
rnAfter installing the SIM card and placing the battery, switch the device to the ON position to start its operation.

rnrn

7. Secure the Cabinet
rnClose the cabinet carefully and tighten all the screws to ensure the device is properly sealed and secured.

rnrn

 

rnrn

The device is now ready to be connected and powered on.

rnrn

rnrn

 

rnrn

NOTE:

rnrn

SIM card insertion/removal must be done when the device is powered off – external voltage disconnected. Otherwise, the SIM card might be damaged or the device will not detect it.

title: Accessories
discription:
1) BLE BEACON

rnrn

IBK-10 is a rugged, high-accuracy BLE beacon built for precise indoor location intelligence. Powered by BLE 5.0, it features IP67-rated durability, long battery endurance, and a laboratory-calibrated temperature sensor. With dual wristband and neckband slots, it is ideal for healthcare, manufacturing, warehouses, logistics centers, industrial safety systems, and smart facility management applications.

rnrn

rnrn

2) BLE FUEL SENSOR

rnrn

FSK-1000 Wireless Fuel Level Sensor delivers precise, capacitive fuel monitoring with effortless Bluetooth BLE connectivity. It can easily be configured and calibrated via your smartphone, and seamlessly be integrated with BLE-enabled telematics and monitoring systems. With its long-lasting battery, the FSK-1000 ensures reliable, hassle-free fuel tracking, keeping your operations efficient, informed, and worry-free at all times.

rnrn

rnrn

3) 1 -WIRE TEMPERATURE SENSOR

rnrn

TSI-10 is a high-precision 1-Wire temperature sensing solution designed for high-accuracy thermal monitoring. Built with a corrosion-resistant stainless-steel probe and fully waterproof enclosure, it delivers dependable performance in harsh conditions. Ideally suited for cold-chain logistics, pharmaceutical storage, food and beverage processing, agriculture, healthcare facilities, and industrial process monitoring requiring consistent temperature control.

rnrn

rnrn

4) TEMPERATURE AND HUMIDITY SENSOR

rnrn

TSI-200 is an industrial-grade temperature and humidity sensor designed for high-precision environmental control. Powered by a 3.3–6V DC supply, it offers < ±0.5°C temperature accuracy, a stable single-bus digital output, and a polymer capacitor sensing element. Well suited for pharmaceutical storage, cold-chain logistics, food and beverage processing, agriculture, healthcare facilities, and industrial monitoring systems requiring dependable and accurate sensing.

rnrn

title: Certifications
discription:
CERTIFICATIONS: CE / RED

rnrn

Radio Equipment Directive (2014/53/EU)

rnrn

The Radio Equipment Directive (RED) 2014/53/EU establishes a regulatory framework to ensure the free movement of radio equipment within the European Single Market. It defines essential requirements related to safety and health, electromagnetic compatibility, and the efficient use of radio spectrum.

rnrn

Description

rnrn

The directive applies to all products that utilize the radio frequency spectrum. It came into force on 13 June 2016, and from 13 June 2017, the updated set of RED requirements became fully applicable to radio equipment.

rnrn

Under the RED directive, manufacturers must demonstrate conformity with the following essential requirements:

rnrn

Article 3.1(a)
rnRadio equipment must be designed and manufactured to ensure the protection of the health and safety of persons and domestic animals, as well as the protection of property. This includes meeting the safety objectives specified in Directive 2014/35/EU (Low Voltage Directive – LVD), although no voltage limits apply under RED.

rnrn

Article 3.1(b)
rnRadio equipment must be constructed to ensure an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), in accordance with the requirements of Directive 2014/30/EU (EMC Directive).

rnrn

Article 3.2
rnRadio equipment must be designed so that it effectively uses and supports the efficient use of the radio spectrum, thereby preventing harmful interference.

rnrn

From 20 December 2020, the standard EN 62368-1 became the only accepted proof of conformity for the LVD safety requirements within the CE RED compliance framework.

rnrn

title: Micro SIM Card Installation and Battery Placement
meta_description: Micro SIM Card Installation and Battery Placement
discription:
To ensure a smooth initial setup of your device, follow these steps to correctly insert the SIM card and place the battery:

rnrn

1. Removing the Back Cover
rnUnscrew all the screws on the back panel to remove the cabinet cover.

rnrn

2. Unlock the cabinet
rnUnlock the lock as shown below to open the cabinet.

rnrn

3. Insert the SIM Card (If using physical SIM)
rnPlace the Micro SIM card into the designated SIM slot as shown in the device manual. Ensure the cut corner of the SIM card is properly aligned with the slot.

rnrn

Note:
rnThe VTC-500 also supports eSIM functionality. If the device is configured with an eSIM profile, inserting a physical SIM card is not required.

rnrn

4. Remove Adhesive Protection
rnPeel off the protective layer from the adhesive tape provided for battery mounting.

rnrn

5. Place the Battery
rnCarefully position the battery inside the VTC-500 casing and press it gently so that the adhesive tape secures the battery firmly in place.

rnrn

6. Power On the Device
rnAfter installing the SIM card and placing the battery, switch the device to the ON position to start its operation.

rnrn

7. Secure the Cabinet
rnClose the cabinet carefully and tighten all the screws to ensure the device is properly sealed and secured.

rnrn

The device is now ready to be connected and powered on.

rnrn

rnrn

NOTE:

rnrn

SIM card insertion/removal must be done when the device is powered off – external voltage disconnected. Otherwise, the SIM card might be damaged or the device will not detect it.

title: Connecting the Device to a PC (Windows)
meta_description: Connecting the Device to a PC (Windows)
discription:
1. Power On the Device
rnPower up the VTC-500 using a DC power supply within the 9–90 V range through the power cable. Once powered, the LED indicators will begin blinking. Refer to “VTC-500 LED Status” for LED indication details.

rnrn

2. Connect the Device to Your Computer
rnThe device can be connected to a computer using either a Micro-USB cable or a Bluetooth ® connection.

rnrn
    rn
  • Using a Micro-USB Cable
    • rn
rnrn

Connect the VTC-500 to your computer using a Micro-USB cable. Ensure that the required USB drivers are installed on your system. Refer to “How to Install USB    Drivers (Windows)” for driver installation instructions.

rnrn
    rn
  • Using Bluetooth ®
    • rn
rnrn

Bluetooth on the VTC-500 is enabled by default. Turn on Bluetooth on your computer and follow these steps:

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    Go to Add Bluetooth or other device and select Bluetooth.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    From the list of available devices, select the device named “VTC500_imei_digits” (do not select the one ending with LE).

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Enter the default password 6906 and click Connect.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Once connected, click Done.

    rn
    • rn
rnrn

The device is now successfully connected and ready to be used on your computer.

title: USB Driver Installation Guide (Windows)
discription:
1. Download the USB Driver
rnDownload the COM port driver from the provided link.
rnNote: The downloadable URL for the COM driver is provided by the R&D team and may vary for each device.

rnrn

2. Extract the Driver Files
rnOnce the download is complete, extract the contents of the compressed folder.

rnrn

3. Run the Driver Installer
rnOpen the extracted folder and run the file VTC-500_AtlantaCOMDriver.exe to start the installation process.

rnrn

4. Start the Installation
rnIn the installation window, click Next to proceed.

rnrn

5. Install the Driver
rnIn the next window, click the Install button to begin installing the driver on your system.

rnrn

6. Complete the Setup
rnThe setup will install the required driver files. Once the installation is completed, a confirmation window will appear. Click Finish to complete the driver installation process.

title: Device Configuration (Windows)
discription:
By default, the VTC-500 device is delivered with factory settings. These settings should be configured according to the specific requirements of the user or application.

rnrn

Device configuration is performed using the Atlanta Configurator software.

rnrn

System Requirements

rnrn

The Atlanta Configurator operates on Microsoft Windows operating systems and requires Microsoft .NET Framework 5.0 (32-bit or 64-bit) to be installed on the computer.

rnrn

Supported operating systems include:

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    Windows Vista

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Windows 7

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Windows 8.1

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Windows 10

    rn
    • rn
rnrn

Ensure that the required .NET Framework version is installed before launching the configurator.

rnrn

Installing and Launching Atlanta Configurator

rnrn
    rn
  1. rn

    Download the latest VTC-500 Configurator from the provided link.

    rn
    2. rn
  2. rn

    The downloaded file will be in a compressed archive format.

    rn
    3. rn
  3. rn

    Extract the contents of the archive.

    rn
    4. rn
  4. rn

    Open the extracted folder and run AtlantaConfigurator.exe.

    rn
    5. rn
rnrn

After launching the software, the interface language can be changed using the language option available in the bottom-right corner of the application.

rnrn

rnrn

Connecting the Device

rnrn

To begin configuration:

rnrn
    rn
  1. rn

    Connect the VTC-500 device to your computer.

    rn
    2. rn
  2. rn

    Open the Atlanta Configurator software.

    rn
    3. rn
  3. rn

    Click on the connected device displayed in the application.

    rn
    4. rn
rnrn

rnrn

Device Status Window

rnrn

Once the connection is successfully established, the Status Window will appear.

rnrn

rnrn

The Status Window provides detailed information about various device parameters, including:

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    GNSS status

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    GSM connectivity

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    I/O parameters

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Maintenance information

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Other operational details

    rn
    • rn
rnrn

Configuration Profiles

rnrn

The VTC-500 device supports one user-editable configuration profile. This profile can be:

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    Loaded from the device

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Modified within the configurator

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Saved back to the device

    rn
    • rn
rnrn

After making any changes to the configuration, you must click Save to Device to apply the new settings.

rnrn

Main Configurator Functions

rnrn

The Atlanta Configurator provides several key functions:

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    Load from Device – Loads the current configuration from the device.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Save to Device – Saves the modified configuration to the device.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Load from File – Loads a configuration stored on your computer.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Save to File – Saves the current configuration to a file for backup or reuse.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Update Firmware – Updates the device firmware.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Read Records – Retrieves stored data records from the device.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Reboot Device – Restarts the device.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Reset Configuration – Restores the device to default factory settings.

    rn
    • rn

Key Configuration Sections

title: Quick SMS configuration guide
discription:
The default configuration ensures optimal track quality and efficient data usage. Follow these steps to quickly set up your device via SMS commands.

rnrn

A. Commands to Change Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Port the Device to a Server

rnrn

   - Command: #SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;

rnrn

   - Example: #SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000; <6906>

rnrn

   - Description: This command directs the VTC-500 device to connect to the server specified by the given IP address and port number. In the example, the device will be configured to communicate with the server at IP 196.168.175.12 and port 20000.

rnrn

 

rnrn

2. To Change the APN Settings

rnrn

- Command: #CONFIG::APN::username::password;

rnrn

- Purpose: Configures the APN settings of the network service provider.

rnrn

- Details:

rnrn

  - APN (Access Point Name): Used to access the GPRS gateway provided by your network operator.

rnrn

  - Username: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Password: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Example: For the Idea network with APN internet, the command would be: #CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

3. Tracking Interval Configuration

rnrn

- Command: WEBSTARTxxx,yyy,zzz,z1z1z1

rnrn

- Purpose: Command to set the tracking interval, and you will get confirmation SMS and then start sending data to the web server, where xxx stands for active(IGN ON) interval, yyy stands for passive(IGN OFF) interval, zzz stands for Main Power Removal interval, and z1z1z1 stands for panic interval.

rnrn

H - Hours, M-Minutes, S- Seconds

rnrn

- Example: WEBSTART030S,030S,030S,030S<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Commands to Check Device Configuration  

rnrn

1. To Check the GPRS Status

rnrn

- Command: GPRSSTATUS<6906>

rnrn

- Purpose: Retrieves the complete status of the device.

rnrn

Description of the reply is as follows:

rnrn

2. To Get GPS Details

rnrn

Send the command `GETGPS` to the VTC-500 device.

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are unreachable: You will receive the message "GPS NOT FOUND."

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are reachable, you will receive a web link to view the location on a map.

rnrn

Additionally, you will receive the following information:

rnrn

- IMEI: Indicates the IMEI number of the device.

rnrn

- ICCID: The ICCID of the SIM card used in the device.

rnrn

- Speed: Indicates the speed of the vehicle in KPH.

rnrn

- Date: The date of the recorded data.

rnrn

- Time: The time of the recorded data in IST.

rnrn

   To view the exact location on Google Maps, click the link in the response or enter the latitude and longitude coordinates separated by a comma (,) in the search bar at [www.maps.google.com](http://www.maps.google.com). This will show the precise location on the map.

rnrn

 

rnrn

3. To Check the Status of the System

rnrn

- Command: SYSSTATUS<6906>

rnrn

- Response: This command provides important system statuses, including:

rnrn

rnrn

rnrn

rnrn

- Internal battery voltage

C. FE<6906>

rnrn

This Command is used to clear the unsent memory data from flash.

rnrn

 

rnrn

D. FR<6906>

rnrn

This Command is used to set factory default values. After this, all the user-configured settings will be erased, and factory-fitted values will be implemented.

rnrn

 

rnrn

E. Default Configuration Settings

rnrn

1. Movement and Ignition Detection

rnrn

- Movement Detection: The device detects vehicle movement using the accelerometer/IGNITION.

rnrn

- Ignition Detection: The ignition is detected by the vehicle's power voltage, which should range between 8 and 90 volts.

rnrn

 

rnrn

2. Device Recording on Movement

rnrn

- Recording Conditions: When the vehicle covers a distance of at least 50 meters while in idle mode, the device will begin tracking the movement of the vehicle.

rnrn

- Stop Detection: The device will mark the vehicle as stopped if it remains stationary for one continuous minute.

rnrn

 

rnrn

3. Device Recording on Stop

rnrn

- Recording Conditions: If the vehicle remains stationary for one continuous minute, the device will mark it as stopped. (speed 0 kmph and no signal from motion sensors/accelerometer)

rnrn

 

rnrn

4. Sending Records to Server

rnrn

- Data Transmission: Once a record is made, it is sent to the server according to the default settings. Data can be sent based on specific criteria such as set time intervals, alerts, angle changes, and distance traveled.

rnrn

 

rnrn

5. Synchronization and Updates

rnrn

After a successful SMS configuration, the VTC-500 device will synchronize its time and update the records to the configured server. Users can modify time intervals and default I/O elements using the Atlanta Configurator tool or additional SMS commands. This ensures that the device remains accurate and up-to-date, providing reliable data for monitoring vehicle movement and status.

title: Mounting Recommendations
discription:
1. Connecting Wires:

rnrn

   - Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.

rnrn

   - Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.

rnrn

   - Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source:

rnrn

   - Power Retention during Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.

rnrn

   - Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.

rnrn

   - Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and protection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire:

rnrn

   - Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.

rnrn

   - Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.

rnrn

   - Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire:

rnrn

   - Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.

rnrn

   - Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

INSTALLATION GUIDE

rnrn

Install the device under the dashboard with a clear sky view. Avoid metal surfaces to prevent signal interference. Ensure the device is securely mounted and properly connected to power and data sources.

rnrn

rnrn

title: Relay Connections
discription:
To properly connect the relay for your device, follow these detailed instructions:

rnrn

1. Pin 85

rnrn

Connect the wire on pin 85 pin with the power source. Ensure that the power supply voltage matches the voltage requirements of your vehicle.

rnrn

2. Pin 87A (Normally Closed) and Pin 30 (Common Connection)

rnrn

   - Pin 30: You need to cut the vehicle’s ignition wire and connect one end to Pin 87A and connect ignition sense wire of the device.

rnrn

   - Pin 87A: Connect it to the ACC (Accessory), Vehicles/ Key Switch wire of your vehicle.

rnrn

3. Pin 86

rnrn

Connect this pin to the device's ignition control wire. This wire controls the relay’s switching based on the ignition status.

rnrn

By following these connections, you ensure that the relay is correctly wired to manage the ignition and power supply for your device, allowing for proper operation and control.

rnrn

 

rnrn

NOTE: Power Supply Connection Guidelines

rnrn

1. Optimal Connection Point

rnrn

When connecting the power supply for the VTC-500 device, it is crucial to select a point with very low impedance on the vehicle's onboard network. Such points are typically found at the battery terminals of the car. This ensures stable voltage supply and minimizes the risk of electrical interference.

rnrn

2. Recommended Connection Methods

rnrn
    rn
  1. Direct Battery Terminal Connection: It is highly recommended to connect the VTC-500’s power wires (GND and POWER) directly to the battery terminals. This direct connection provides a reliable and stable power source for the device.
    2. rn
  2. Fuse Box Connection: Alternatively, you can connect the wires to the main POWER cable inside the vehicle's fuse box. Ensure that the fuse box is connected to the vehicle's computer power supply. This method also provides a controlled power supply environment.
    3. rn
rnrn

3. Ground Connection Considerations

rnrn

- GND Wire Connection: The GND wire must be connected to a designated point specifically designed for connecting vehicle computer grounds. Avoid arbitrary grounding to the car's mass, as this can introduce unpredictable static and dynamic potentials, potentially leading to unstable operation or failure of the VTC-500 device.

rnrn

By adhering to these detailed connection guidelines, you can ensure the proper and reliable operation of the VTC-500 device within your vehicle's electrical system. Always prioritize stable connections and avoid any practices that could compromise the device's performance or safety.

rnrn

title: Sleep Modes
discription:
The VTC-500 device supports four different sleep modes:

rnrn
    rn
  • GPS Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Online Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
  • Ultra Deep Sleep Mode
    • rn
rnrn

These modes are designed to reduce the device’s power consumption when the vehicle is not in operation.

rnrn

1. GPS Sleep Mode

rnrn

The VTC-500 can enter GPS Sleep Mode if this mode is enabled in the configuration settings.

rnrn

The sleep timeout starts counting once the device enters STOP mode. After the configured timeout is reached and all required conditions for GPS Sleep Mode are satisfied, the device transitions into sleep mode.

rnrn

When operating in GPS Sleep Mode, the VTC-500 turns off the GPS module while continuing to create new periodic records. This helps reduce power consumption and conserves the vehicle battery.

rnrn

The VTC-500 enters GPS Sleep Mode when all of the following conditions are met:

rnrn
    rn
  • The device is configured to operate in GPS Sleep Mode, and the sleep timeout has been reached.
    • rn
  • The device time must be synchronized with GPS satellites. Starting from firmware ATL-VTC-500-V0.2, this requirement depends on the “Records saving/sending without TS” parameter:rn
      rn
    • After Position Fix – The VTC-500 time is synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix is obtained.
      • rn
    • After Time Sync – The VTC-500 time is synchronized via NTP, NITZ, or GNSS satellites.
      • rn
    • Always – The VTC-500 will enter sleep mode even without time synchronization or GPS fix.
      • rn
    rn
    • rn
  • No movement is detected by the accelerometer or the configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is off.
    • rn
  • No SMS messages are being received.
    • rn
rnrn

Note: In firmware versions older than ATL-VTC-500-V0.2.0, the device time must be synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix must be obtained before the device can enter GPS Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-500 exits GPS Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

2. Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

When the VTC-500 enters Deep Sleep Mode, the GNSS receiver is set to sleep mode, and the GSM/GPRS module is turned off. As a result, it is not possible to wake the device via SMS.

rnrn

Even in this mode, the device continues to save records with the last known coordinates and sends them to the AVL server. To transmit data, the GSM/GPRS module is temporarily turned on and then switched off again after the data is sent. This approach helps reduce power consumption and conserve the vehicle’s battery.

rnrn

Power saving in Deep Sleep Mode depends on two configurable parameters:

rnrn
    rn
  • Send Period
    • rn
  • Minimum Record Saving Period under “X on Stop Mode”
    • rn
rnrn

When records are successfully sent while in Deep Sleep Mode, the Open Link Timeout counter is skipped, allowing the VTC-500 to immediately return to Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

Because many functions are disabled during Deep Sleep Mode, the following I/O elements are not included in records generated in this mode:

rnrn
    rn
  • GSM Signal
    • rn
  • GNSS Status
    • rn
  • GNSS PDOP
    • rn
  • GNSS HDOP
    • rn
  • GSM CellID
    • rn
  • GSM Area Code
    • rn
  • Active GSM Operator
    • rn
  • Trip Odometer
    • rn
  • Total Odometer
    • rn
  • Speed
    • rn
  • Fuel Rate GPS
    • rn
  • Fuel Used GPS
    • rn
  • ICCID
    • rn
rnrn

The VTC-500 can enter Deep Sleep Mode when all of the following conditions are satisfied:

rnrn
    rn
  • The device is configured for Deep Sleep Mode, and the sleep timeout has been reached.
    • rn
  • The device time must be synchronized with GPS satellites. Starting from firmware ATL-VTC-500-V0.2, this depends on the “Records saving/sending without TS” parameter:rn
      rn
    • After Position Fix – VTC-500 time is synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix is obtained.
      • rn
    • After Time Sync – VTC-500 time is synchronized through NTP, NITZ, or GNSS satellites.
      • rn
    • Always – VTC-500 can enter sleep mode without time synchronization or GPS fix.
      • rn
    rn
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is off.
    • rn
  • No movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Minimum Record Saving Period (Data Acquisition Mode settings) must be greater than the Open Link Timeout parameter, allowing the VTC-500 to close the GPRS link.
    • rn
  • The difference between Send Period (Data Acquisition Mode settings) and Open Link Timeout must be more than 90 seconds, allowing the device to close the GPRS link within at least 90 seconds.
    • rn
  • No SMS messages are being received.
    • rn
  • Data socket(s) are closed.
    • rn
  • Data sending is not in progress.
    • rn
  • FOTA is not in progress.
    • rn
rnrn

Note: In firmware versions older than ATL-VTC-500-V0.2, the device time must be synchronized with GNSS satellites, and a GPS fix must be obtained before the device can enter Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-500 exits Deep Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

3. Online Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

In Online Deep Sleep Mode, the VTC-500 operates similarly to Deep Sleep Mode, but remains registered on the GSM network. The GSM module stays powered, resulting in higher power consumption compared to standard Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

In this mode, the device can:

rnrn
    rn
  • Send and receive SMS messages
    • rn
  • Make or receive calls
    • rn
rnrn

Additionally, if a GPRS context was previously opened, it remains active and is not closed.

rnrn

The conditions required to enter Online Deep Sleep Mode are the same as those for entering Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-500 exits Online Deep Sleep Mode if one of the following conditions occurs:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer or configured movement source.
    • rn
  • Ignition (configured ignition source) is turned on.
    • rn
rnrn

4. Ultra Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

In Ultra Deep Sleep Mode, both the GPS module and GSM modem are turned off, and most device functions are suspended to achieve maximum battery saving.

rnrn

The conditions required to enter Ultra Deep Sleep Mode are the same as those for entering Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

The VTC-500 exits Ultra Deep Sleep Mode only when:

rnrn
    rn
  • Movement is detected by the accelerometer, or
    • rn
  • I/O inputs detect activity
    • rn
rnrn

In this mode, movement source configuration and ignition source configuration are not taken into account.

title: SMS/GPRS Command Overview
discription:
The VTC-500 device is a versatile communication tool designed to receive commands via GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) and SMS (Short Message Service). GPRS enables the device to maintain a continuous internet connection for real-time data transmission and command reception, making it ideal for remote monitoring and control applications. SMS provides a reliable alternative for sending commands when GPRS connectivity is unavailable or limited.

rnrn

All commands are case sensitive.  

rnrn

While SMS commands are sent using recharges, GPRS commands are sent via the internet. Another difference lies in their syntax. But their working & flow of execution of the task is the same. Clients can make use of the FOTAWEB platform, which is an additional feature provided by the company for easy and fast configuration of devices on which these GPRS commands can be sent.

title: Certifications
discription:
CERTIFICATIONS: CE / RED

rnrn

Radio Equipment Directive (2014/53/EU)

rnrn

The Radio Equipment Directive (RED) 2014/53/EU establishes a regulatory framework to ensure the free movement of radio equipment within the European Single Market. It defines essential requirements related to safety and health, electromagnetic compatibility, and the efficient use of radio spectrum.

rnrn

Description

rnrn

The directive applies to all products that utilize the radio frequency spectrum. It came into force on 13 June 2016, and from 13 June 2017, the updated set of RED requirements became fully applicable to radio equipment.

rnrn

Under the RED directive, manufacturers must demonstrate conformity with the following essential requirements:

rnrn

Article 3.1(a)
rnRadio equipment must be designed and manufactured to ensure the protection of the health and safety of persons and domestic animals, as well as the protection of property. This includes meeting the safety objectives specified in Directive 2014/35/EU (Low Voltage Directive – LVD), although no voltage limits apply under RED.

rnrn

Article 3.1(b)
rnRadio equipment must be constructed to ensure an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), in accordance with the requirements of Directive 2014/30/EU (EMC Directive).

rnrn

Article 3.2
rnRadio equipment must be designed so that it effectively uses and supports the efficient use of the radio spectrum, thereby preventing harmful interference.

rnrn

From 20 December 2020, the standard EN 62368-1 became the only accepted proof of conformity for the LVD safety requirements within the CE RED compliance framework.

rnrn

title: Accessories
discription:
1) BLE BEACON

rnrn

IBK-10 is a rugged, high-accuracy BLE beacon built for precise indoor location intelligence. Powered by BLE 5.0, it features IP67-rated durability, long battery endurance, and a laboratory-calibrated temperature sensor. With dual wristband and neckband slots, it is ideal for healthcare, manufacturing, warehouses, logistics centers, industrial safety systems, and smart facility management applications.

rnrn

rnrn

2) BLE FUEL SENSOR

rnrn

FSK-1000 Wireless Fuel Level Sensor delivers precise, capacitive fuel monitoring with effortless Bluetooth BLE connectivity. It can easily be configured and calibrated via your smartphone, and seamlessly be integrated with BLE-enabled telematics and monitoring systems. With its long-lasting battery, the FSK-1000 ensures reliable, hassle-free fuel tracking, keeping your operations efficient, informed, and worry-free at all times.

rnrn

rnrn

3) 1 -WIRE TEMPERATURE SENSOR

rnrn

TSI-10 is a high-precision 1-Wire temperature sensing solution designed for high-accuracy thermal monitoring. Built with a corrosion-resistant stainless-steel probe and fully waterproof enclosure, it delivers dependable performance in harsh conditions. Ideally suited for cold-chain logistics, pharmaceutical storage, food and beverage processing, agriculture, healthcare facilities, and industrial process monitoring requiring consistent temperature control.

rnrn

rnrn

4) TEMPERATURE AND HUMIDITY SENSOR

rnrn

TSI-200 is an industrial-grade temperature and humidity sensor designed for high-precision environmental control. Powered by a 3.3–6V DC supply, it offers < ±0.5°C temperature accuracy, a stable single-bus digital output, and a polymer capacitor sensing element. Well suited for pharmaceutical storage, cold-chain logistics, food and beverage processing, agriculture, healthcare facilities, and industrial monitoring systems requiring dependable and accurate sensing.

title: Certifications
discription:
CERTIFICATIONS: CE / RED

rnrn

Radio Equipment Directive (2014/53/EU)

rnrn

The Radio Equipment Directive (RED) 2014/53/EU establishes a regulatory framework to ensure the free movement of radio equipment within the European Single Market. It defines essential requirements related to safety and health, electromagnetic compatibility, and the efficient use of radio spectrum.

rnrn

Description

rnrn

The directive applies to all products that utilize the radio frequency spectrum. It came into force on 13 June 2016, and from 13 June 2017, the updated set of RED requirements became fully applicable to radio equipment.

rnrn

Under the RED directive, manufacturers must demonstrate conformity with the following essential requirements:

rnrn

Article 3.1(a)
rnRadio equipment must be designed and manufactured to ensure the protection of the health and safety of persons and domestic animals, as well as the protection of property. This includes meeting the safety objectives specified in Directive 2014/35/EU (Low Voltage Directive – LVD), although no voltage limits apply under RED.

rnrn

Article 3.1(b)
rnRadio equipment must be constructed to ensure an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), in accordance with the requirements of Directive 2014/30/EU (EMC Directive).

rnrn

Article 3.2
rnRadio equipment must be designed so that it effectively uses and supports the efficient use of the radio spectrum, thereby preventing harmful interference.

rnrn

From 20 December 2020, the standard EN 62368-1 became the only accepted proof of conformity for the LVD safety requirements within the CE RED compliance framework.

rnrn

Standards Applied

title: Certifications
discription:
CERTIFICATIONS: CE / RED

rnrn

Radio Equipment Directive (2014/53/EU)

rnrn

The Radio Equipment Directive (RED) 2014/53/EU establishes a regulatory framework to ensure the free movement of radio equipment within the European Single Market. It defines essential requirements related to safety and health, electromagnetic compatibility, and the efficient use of radio spectrum.

rnrn

Description

rnrn

The directive applies to all products that utilize the radio frequency spectrum. It came into force on 13 June 2016, and from 13 June 2017, the updated set of RED requirements became fully applicable to radio equipment.

rnrn

Under the RED directive, manufacturers must demonstrate conformity with the following essential requirements:

rnrn

Article 3.1(a)
rnRadio equipment must be designed and manufactured to ensure the protection of the health and safety of persons and domestic animals, as well as the protection of property. This includes meeting the safety objectives specified in Directive 2014/35/EU (Low Voltage Directive – LVD), although no voltage limits apply under RED.

rnrn

Article 3.1(b)
rnRadio equipment must be constructed to ensure an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), in accordance with the requirements of Directive 2014/30/EU (EMC Directive).

rnrn

Article 3.2
rnRadio equipment must be designed so that it effectively uses and supports the efficient use of the radio spectrum, thereby preventing harmful interference.

rnrn

From 20 December 2020, the standard EN 62368-1 became the only accepted proof of conformity for the LVD safety requirements within the CE RED compliance framework.

rnrn

rnrn

title: SMS/GPRS Command Overview
discription:
The VTC-100 device is a versatile communication tool designed to receive commands via GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) and SMS (Short Message Service). GPRS enables the device to maintain a continuous internet connection for real-time data transmission and command reception, making it ideal for remote monitoring and control applications. SMS provides a reliable alternative for sending commands when GPRS connectivity is unavailable or limited.

rnrn

All commands are case sensitive.  

rnrn

While SMS commands are sent using recharges, GPRS commands are sent via the internet. Another difference lies in their syntax. But their working & flow of execution of the task is the same. Clients can make use of the FOTAWEB platform, which is an additional feature provided by the company for easy and fast configuration of devices on which these GPRS commands can be sent.

Server Settings#SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;<password>Point the device to a server with a specified IP and port.#SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000;<6906>
#SERVERCHANGE1::IP::PORT;<password>Point the device to the second server with the specified IP and port. To enable the dual IP data sending mode#SERVERCHANGE1::196.168.175.12::20000;<6906>
#SERVERCHANGE1::--;<6906>To remove the second IP, disable the Dual IP data sending mode#SERVERCHANGE1::--;<6906>
GPRS / APN Settings#CONFIG::APN::username::password;<password>Configure the GPRS account with APN, username, and password provided by the network operator.#CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>
#CONFIG?<password>Check the APN configuration of the device. Responds with saved GPRS APN, username, and password.#CONFIG?<6906>
Odometer ConfigurationSETODO::xxxxx;<password>Set the odometer to the present vehicle reading.SETODO::12345;<6906>
SETODO?<password>Get the current odometer value.SETODO?<6906>
Harsh Event CommandsHT::HA::HB::angle;<password>This command is used to set threshold values for sensing harsh turns, harsh braking, and harsh accelerationHT::005::005::020;<6906>
HT?<password>Enquire current harsh event thresholds.HT?<6906>
HT--;<password>Remove harsh event thresholds.HT--;<6909>
Overspeed AlertSPEED?<password>Check overspeed threshold.SPEED?<6906>
SPEED--;<password>Remove overspeed threshold.SPEED--;<6906>
SPEED::XXX;<password>Set the overspeed limit in KMPH.SPEED::100;<6906>
GMT ShiftGMS::xxxxx;<password>Set the GMT offset in minutes.GMT::330;<6906>
Password ChangePW::NewPassword;<DefaultPassword>Change the default password to a custom one. The password should be a four-digit number.PW::1234;<6906>
Vehicle ImmobilizerARM<password>Activate ARM mode. Cuts Ignition/Turn ON relay.ARM<6906>
DISARM<password>Deactivate ARM mode. Connect Ignition/Turn OFF Relay.DISARM<6906>
PPI ConfigurationWEBSTART<xxx/H/M/S>,<yyy/H/M/S>,<zzz/H/M/S>,<z1z1z1/H/M/S><password>Command to set the tracking interval, and you will get a confirmation SMS, and then start sending data to our web server, where xxx stands for active(IGN ON) interval, yyy stands for passive(IGN OFF) interval, zzz stands for Main Power Removal interval, and z1z1z1 stands for panic interval.WEBSTART030S,030S,030S,030S<6906>
Distance-Based TrackingDBT<xxxM/K><password>Enable distance-based tracking. Sends data to the server after covering the set distance and on deviation from the normal course. M-Meters, K-KilometersDBT500M<6906>
SDBT<password>Stop distance and angle-based tracking.SDBT<6906>
Output ON/OFFGOUTON<password>The device will lock the motor, and the Motor will not work after this command.GOUTON<6909>
GOUTOFF<password>The device will unlock the motor, and the Motor starts working GOUTOFF<6909>
BLE Sensor SettingsBLEMAC::MAC::X;<password>To set the MAC address of sensors to capture the data. Here, MAC stands for the MAC address of the sensor, and X stands for sensor type.

rn X=0  No lock(Always in motion)
rn X=1 Lock on IGNITION
rn X=2 Lock on Accelerometer		LOCKLATLONG::2;<password>

Firmware VersionVERSION<password>Check firmware & hardware version.VERSION<6906>

title: Micro SIM Card Installation and Battery Placement
meta_description: Micro SIM Card Installation and Battery Placement
discription:
To ensure a smooth initial setup of your device, follow these steps to insert the SIM card and place the battery correctly:

rnrn

1. Remove the Back Cover
rnUnscrew all the screws on the back panel to remove the cabinet cover.

rnrn

2. Unlock the cabinet
rnUnlock the lock as shown below to open the cabinet.

rnrn

3. Insert the SIM Card (If using a physical SIM)
rnPlace the Micro SIM card into the designated SIM slot as shown in the device manual. Ensure the cut corner of the SIM card is properly aligned with the slot.

rnrn

4. Remove Adhesive Protection
rnPeel off the protective layer from the adhesive tape provided for battery mounting.

rnrn

5. Place the Battery
rnCarefully position the battery inside the VTC-300 casing and press it gently until the adhesive tape secures it firmly in place.

rnrn

6. Power On the Device
rnAfter installing the SIM card and placing the battery, switch the device to the ON position to start its operation.

rnrn

7. Secure the Cabinet
rnClose the cabinet carefully and tighten all the screws to ensure the device is properly sealed and secured.

rnrn

The device is now ready to be connected and powered on.

rnrn

rnrn

NOTE:

rnrn

SIM card insertion/removal must be done when the device is powered off – external voltage disconnected. Otherwise, the SIM card might be damaged or the device will not detect it.

title: Quick SMS configuration guide
discription:
The default configuration ensures optimal track quality and efficient data usage. Follow these steps to quickly set up your device via SMS commands.

rnrn

A. Commands to Change Device Configuration

rnrn

1. To Port the Device to a Server

rnrn

   - Command: #SERVERCHANGE::IP::PORT;

rnrn

   - Example: #SERVERCHANGE::196.168.175.12::20000; <6906>

rnrn

   - Description: This command directs the VTC-300 device to connect to the server specified by the given IP address and port number. In the example, the device will be configured to communicate with the server at IP 196.168.175.12 and port 20000.

rnrn

 

rnrn

2. To Change the APN Settings

rnrn

- Command: #CONFIG::APN::username::password;

rnrn

- Purpose: Configures the APN settings of the network service provider.

rnrn

- Details:

rnrn

  - APN (Access Point Name): Used to access the GPRS gateway provided by your network operator.

rnrn

  - Username: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Password: Provided by your network operator (leave blank if not required).

rnrn

  - Example: For the Idea network with APN internet, the command would be: #CONFIG::internet::::;<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

3. Tracking Interval Configuration

rnrn

- Command: WEBSTARTxxx,yyy,zzz,z1z1z1

rnrn

- Purpose: Command to set the tracking interval, and you will get confirmation SMS and then start sending data to the web server, where xxx stands for active(IGN ON) interval, yyy stands for passive(IGN OFF) interval, zzz stands for Main Power Removal interval, and z1z1z1 stands for panic interval.

rnrn

H - Hours, M-Minutes, S- Seconds

rnrn

- Example: WEBSTART030S,030S,030S,030S<6906>

rnrn

 

rnrn

B. Commands to Check Device Configuration  

rnrn

1. To Check the GPRS Status

rnrn

- Command: GPRSSTATUS<6906>

rnrn

- Purpose: Retrieves the complete status of the device.

rnrn

2. To Get GPS Details

rnrn

Send the command `GETGPS` to the VTC-300 device.

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are unreachable: You will receive the message "GPS NOT FOUND."

rnrn

- If GPS satellites are reachable, you will receive a web link to view the location on a map.

rnrn

Additionally, you will receive the following information:

rnrn

- Time: The time of the recorded data in IST.

rnrn

   To view the exact location on Google Maps, click the link in the response or enter the latitude and longitude coordinates separated by a comma (,) in the search bar at [www.maps.google.com](http://www.maps.google.com). This will show the precise location on the map.

rnrn

 

rnrn

E. Default Configuration Settings

rnrn

1. Movement and Ignition Detection

rnrn

- Movement Detection: The device detects vehicle movement using the accelerometer/IGNITION.

rnrn

- Ignition Detection: The ignition is detected by the vehicle's power voltage, which should range between 8 and 90 volts.

rnrn

2. Device Recording on Movement

rnrn

- Recording Conditions: When the vehicle covers a distance of at least 50 meters while in idle mode, the device will begin tracking the movement of the vehicle.

rnrn

- Stop Detection: The device will mark the vehicle as stopped if it remains stationary for one continuous minute.

rnrn

3. Device Recording on Stop

rnrn

- Recording Conditions: If the vehicle remains stationary for one continuous minute, the device will mark it as stopped. (speed 0 kmph and no signal from motion sensors/accelerometer)

rnrn

4. Sending Records to Server

rnrn

- Data Transmission: Once a record is made, it is sent to the server according to the default settings. Data can be sent based on specific criteria such as set time intervals, alerts, angle changes, and distance traveled.

rnrn

5. Synchronization and Updates

rnrn

After a successful SMS configuration, the VTC-300 device will synchronize its time and update the records to the configured server. Users can modify time intervals and default I/O elements using the Atlanta Configurator tool or additional SMS commands. This ensures that the device remains accurate and up-to-date, providing reliable data for monitoring vehicle movement and status.

title: Mounting Recommendations
discription:
1. Connecting Wires:

rnrn

   - Secure Placement: Ensure that wires are securely fastened to stable, immovable parts of the vehicle. This prevents them from becoming loose or moving around, which could cause damage or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Avoid Heat and Movement: Keep wires away from sources of heat and moving components within the vehicle. Heat can degrade insulation and cause electrical issues, while movement can lead to wear and eventual failure of the wires.

rnrn

   - Insulation Protection: It's crucial that wires have proper insulation throughout their length. If any factory-provided insulation is removed during installation, replace it with suitable insulation material to prevent electrical shorts or other hazards.

rnrn

   - Environmental Protection: If wires are installed in exterior locations or areas prone to heat, humidity, or dirt, additional protective measures should be taken. This includes ensuring the wires are well-isolated and securely fastened to prevent exposure to elements that could compromise their integrity.

rnrn

2. Connecting Power Source:

rnrn

   - Power Retention during Sleep Mode: After the car's computer enters sleep mode, certain circuits may still have power for a period (typically 5 to 30 minutes). This residual power can affect how devices connected to the car's electrical system operate and should be considered during installation.

rnrn

   - Voltage Stability: Always measure the voltage after connecting devices to ensure it remains stable and within safe operating limits. Fluctuations in voltage can affect the performance and longevity of connected electrical components.

rnrn

   - Fuse Box Connection: It's recommended to connect devices to the main power cable within the fuse box. This ensures a reliable and regulated power supply, as the fuse box manages electrical distribution and protection throughout the vehicle.

rnrn

3. Connecting Ignition Wire:

rnrn

   - Verification of Ignition Wire: Verify that the wire chosen for ignition connection maintains power consistently, especially after starting the engine. This ensures that connected devices receive power only when the ignition is on, preventing drain on the battery during engine off periods.

rnrn

   - Differentiating from ACC Wire: An ignition wire differs from an accessory (ACC) wire, which typically powers vehicle electronics in the first key position without starting the engine. Carefully identify and use the correct wire to ensure devices operate as intended.

rnrn

   - Power Availability Check: Confirm that power remains available on the ignition wire even when other vehicle accessories are turned off. This ensures uninterrupted operation of connected devices without relying on transient power sources.

rnrn

4. Connecting Ground Wire:

rnrn

   - Proper Grounding Location: Connect the ground wire securely to the vehicle frame or to metal components directly fixed to the frame. The vehicle frame serves as a reliable ground point, ensuring stable electrical grounding for connected devices.

rnrn

   - Bolting and Loop Connection: When attaching the ground wire with a bolt, ensure that the loop at the end of the wire securely fastens to the designated grounding point. This prevents loose connections that could lead to electrical instability or malfunction.

rnrn

   - Surface Preparation: To enhance conductivity and ensure a solid ground connection, remove any paint or coatings from the contact area where the ground wire attaches to the vehicle frame. This improves the electrical contact and reduces the risk of poor grounding affecting device performance.

rnrn

 

rnrn

INSTALLATION GUIDE

rnrn

Install the device under the dashboard with a clear sky view. Avoid metal surfaces to prevent signal interference. Ensure the device is securely mounted and properly connected to power and data sources.

rnrn

title: Relay Connections
discription:
To properly connect the relay for your device, follow these detailed instructions:

rnrn

1. Pin 85

rnrn

Connect the wire on pin 85 pin with the power source. Ensure that the power supply voltage matches the voltage requirements of your vehicle.

rnrn

2. Pin 87A (Normally Closed) and Pin 30 (Common Connection)

rnrn

   - Pin 30: You need to cut the vehicle’s ignition wire and connect one end to Pin 87A and connect the ignition sense wire of the device.

rnrn

   - Pin 87A: Connect it to the ACC (Accessory), Vehicles/ Key Switch wire of your vehicle.

rnrn

3. Pin 86

rnrn

Connect this pin to the device's ignition control wire. This wire controls the relay’s switching based on the ignition status.

rnrn

By following these connections, you ensure that the relay is correctly wired to manage the ignition and power supply for your device, allowing for proper operation and control.

rnrn

 

rnrn

NOTE: Power Supply Connection Guidelines

rnrn

1. Optimal Connection Point

rnrn

When connecting the power supply for the VTC-300 device, it is crucial to select a point with very low impedance on the vehicle's onboard network. Such points are typically found at the battery terminals of the car. This ensures stable voltage supply and minimizes the risk of electrical interference.

rnrn

2. Recommended Connection Methods

rnrn
    rn
  1. Direct Battery Terminal Connection: It is highly recommended to connect the VTC-300’s power wires (GND and POWER) directly to the battery terminals. This direct connection provides a reliable and stable power source for the device.
    2. rn
  2. Fuse Box Connection: Alternatively, you can connect the wires to the main POWER cable inside the vehicle's fuse box. Ensure that the fuse box is connected to the vehicle's computer power supply. This method also provides a controlled power supply environment.
    3. rn
rnrn

3. Ground Connection Considerations

rnrn

- GND Wire Connection: The GND wire must be connected to a designated point specifically designed for connecting vehicle computer grounds. Avoid arbitrary grounding to the car's mass, as this can introduce unpredictable static and dynamic potentials, potentially leading to unstable operation or failure of the VTC-300 device.

rnrn

By adhering to these detailed connection guidelines, you can ensure the proper and reliable operation of the VTC-300 device within your vehicle's electrical system. Always prioritize stable connections and avoid any practices that could compromise the device's performance or safety.

title: Safety information and precautions
discription:
Operating the VTC-300 device safely requires careful attention to the following guidelines and recommendations. Adhering to these instructions will help you avoid hazardous situations and ensure the optimal performance of your device. Please read and follow these instructions meticulously before operating the device.

rnrn

A) Safety instructions

rnrn

1. Power Specifications:

rnrn
    rn
  • The VTC-300 device operates on a nominal voltage of +12 VDC/+24 VDC/+48 VDC/+74 VDC.
    • rn
rnrn
    rn
  • The allowable voltage range for safe operation is between +9 V DC and +90 V DC.
    • rn
rnrn

2. Transportation and Handling

rnrn
    rn
  • To prevent mechanical damage during transportation, ensure that the device is packaged in an impact-resistant container.
    • rn
  • When setting up the device, place it in a location where the LED indicators are clearly visible. These indicators provide essential information about the device's operational status.
    • rn
rnrn

3. Connection and Disconnection Procedures

rnrn
    rn
  • When connecting the wiring harness to the vehicle, make sure to disconnect the relevant jumpers from the vehicle's power supply first.
    • rn
  • Before removing the device from the vehicle, always disconnect the wiring harness to prevent any electrical hazards.
    • rn
rnrn

4. Mounting Instructions

rnrn
    rn
  • The device should be installed in a restricted access area, ensuring that it remains out of reach of the operator during normal operation.
    • rn
  • Secure the device firmly in its designated location to prevent any accidental displacement.
    • rn
  • The device should be installed with a sky view and kept away from metal surfaces.
    • rn
rnrn

5. Water Exposure

rnrn
    rn
  • Avoid exposing the device directly to water, as it is not built to withstand water exposure and may malfunction as a result.
    • rn
rnrn

6. Installation Conditions

rnrn
    rn
  • Installation and handling of the device should not be performed during a lightning storm to avoid the risk of electrical shock or damage.
    • rn
rnrn

 

rnrn

B) PREVENTIVE MEASURES

rnrn

1. Interference and Placement

rnrn

title: Certifications
discription:
CERTIFICATIONS: CE / RED

rnrn

Radio Equipment Directive (2014/53/EU)

rnrn

The Radio Equipment Directive (RED) 2014/53/EU establishes a regulatory framework to ensure the free movement of radio equipment within the European Single Market. It defines essential requirements related to safety and health, electromagnetic compatibility, and the efficient use of radio spectrum.

rnrn

Description

rnrn

The directive applies to all products that utilize the radio frequency spectrum. It came into force on 13 June 2016, and from 13 June 2017, the updated set of RED requirements became fully applicable to radio equipment.

rnrn

Under the RED directive, manufacturers must demonstrate conformity with the following essential requirements:

rnrn

Article 3.1(a)
rnRadio equipment must be designed and manufactured to ensure the protection of the health and safety of persons and domestic animals, as well as the protection of property. This includes meeting the safety objectives specified in Directive 2014/35/EU (Low Voltage Directive – LVD), although no voltage limits apply under RED.

rnrn

Article 3.1(b)
rnRadio equipment must be constructed to ensure an adequate level of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), in accordance with the requirements of Directive 2014/30/EU (EMC Directive).

rnrn

Article 3.2
rnRadio equipment must be designed so that it effectively uses and supports the efficient use of the radio spectrum, thereby preventing harmful interference.

rnrn

From 20 December 2020, the standard EN 62368-1 became the only accepted proof of conformity for the LVD safety requirements within the CE RED compliance framework.

rnrn

title: How to activate IBK-10 beacon
discription:
Press the button to sleeping device and wait for LED to blink.

rnrn

Attach photo

rnrn

Now device is discoverable, scannable, connectable via BLE.

title: Device Operations
discription:
1) Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

By default, the beacon remains in Deep Sleep Mode.

rnrn

Purpose:

rnrn
    rn
  • Ultra-low power consumption
    • rn
  • Extended battery life
    • rn
  • Prevent unauthorized configuration
    • rn
rnrn

2) Wake-up / Configuration Mode

rnrn

Press the beacon button.

rnrn

The beacon will:

rnrn
    rn
  • Wake from Deep Sleep.
    • rn
  • Start BLE advertising.
    • rn
  • Remain discoverable for 10 seconds.
    • rn
rnrn

If a BLE client connects during this period:

rnrn
    rn
  • Pairing is completed.
    • rn
  • Configuration window is extended by 30 seconds.
    • rn
rnrn

During this period users can:

rnrn
    rn
  • Configure beacon parameters
    • rn
  • Change advertising behavior
    • rn
  • Perform firmware upgrades
    • rn
  • Configure pairing settings
    • rn
  • Return beacon to Deep Sleep mode
    • rn

title: Beacon Configuration
discription:
Once beacon in Configuration Mode and are ready to perform out of the box.

rnrn

Default basic Sensor settings are set to:

rnrn
    rn
  • Transmitting at 0 dBm power.
    • rn
  • Data advertising at 5 min intervals. 
    • rn
rnrn

If you would like to change these settings you will need to: 

rnrn
    rn
  • Download and install BLE APP to change sensor settings. 
    • rn
  • With the application you will be able to scan for visible Beacon, check their status, connect for configuration using configuration commands. 
    • rn

discription:
1) Advertising Configuration

rnrn

Used to configure:

rnrn
    rn
  • Sleep Time
    • rn
  • Number of Advertising Packets
    • rn
  • Time Gap Between Advertisements
    • rn
rnrn

Command Format

rnrn

Config::sleeptime::no_of_adv_packets::time_between_packets;

rnrn

Parameters

rnrnrn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn
ParameterDescription

no_of_adv_packetsNumber of advertisements transmitted in one cycle
time_between_packetsDelay between advertisements

rnrn

rnrn
    rn

    • rn

    • rn

    • rn

2) Pairing Configuration

rnrn

Used to configure pairing and connection windows.

rnrn

rnrn

rnrn

  • Pairing Window = 10 sec
    • rn

    • rn
rnrn

3) Firmware Upgrade Command

rnrn

Used to trigger firmware download and update.

rnrn

Command Format

rnrn

#REPROGRAM::IP Address::Username::Password::Filename;

Parameters

rnrnrn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn rn

Example

rnrn

4) Enter Deep Sleep Mode

rnrn

Returns beacon to Hibernate Mode.

rnrn

Command Format

rnrn

SleepON;

rnrn

Example

rnrn

SleepON;1234

rnrn

After execution:

rnrn
    rn
  • Beacon disconnects
    • rn
  • Advertising stops
    • rn
  • Device enters Deep Sleep
    • rn

title: Overview
discription:
The IBK-10 is a rugged Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE 5.0) beacon designed for indoor location intelligence, personnel tracking, asset monitoring, healthcare, industrial safety, warehousing, and smart facility management applications. It features temperature sensing, humidity monitoring, battery status reporting, and configurable advertising behavior. 

rnrn

Introduction

rnrn

The IBK-10 operates in an ultra-low-power architecture where the device normally remains in Deep Sleep (Hibernate) Mode to maximize battery life.
rnWhen the user presses the onboard button, the beacon wakes up and enters Client/Configuration Mode, allowing configuration, pairing, and firmware updates.

rnrn

Key Features

rnrn
    rn
  • BLE 5.0 Beacon
    • rn
  • Deep Sleep / Hibernate operation
    • rn
  • Configurable advertising interval
    • rn
  • Configurable number of advertising packets
    • rn
  • Configurable sleep time
    • rn
  • Temperature sensing
    • rn
  • Humidity sensing
    • rn
  • Battery monitoring
    • rn
  • Panic button detection
    • rn
  • OTA Firmware Upgrade support
    • rn
  • IP67 enclosure
    • rn
  • Wristband and Neckband mounting support
    • rn

title: Beacon not visible
discription:

rnrn
    rn
  • Device is in Deep Sleep Mode.
    • rn
  • Pairing window expired.
    • rn
  • Battery discharged.
    • rn
rnrn

Solution:

rnrn
    rn
  • Press beacon button.
    • rn
  • Scan again within 10 seconds.
    • rn
  • Verify battery voltage.
    • rn
